# The component reference

<!-- Generated by `Maintain/Script/Reference.mjs` from `Source/Content/Specimen/*.ts`.
     Do not edit by hand: an edit here is a second opinion about a component, and
     the next regeneration would delete it. Change the family module, then run
     the script. -->

This is the document a contributor reads before touching a component. It states,
for each of the 10 families of the document, the same five
things in the same order:

1. **what the family is for** - the sentence its band argues, and what it is read for;
2. **its slots** - the parts a page may mount, each with the file it lives in;
3. **what it is asked** - the states it is conditioned on, and the shapes and
   contexts it is composed at, with the figure each column is built by;
4. **what it may never be** - the sentences the family's own matrix uses to mark
   a combination impossible, collected rather than written;
5. **the row that proves it** - one live specimen that shows the family
   surviving the case its own subject says it is worst at.

Every figure, every column, every prohibition and every matrix cell is read from
the ten family modules (`Source/Content/Specimen/<Family>.ts`), which are the
same tables `/Specimen` and `/Specimen/States` read. Nothing here is a second
claim about a component: a cell in this document and a cell on the family's
matrix are the same cell, read twice.

**How to use it.** Find the family, read _what it is for_ and _what it may never
be_ before you open a file. If you are adding a combination, check the matrix
first: if the cell is `N/A`, the family has already written the sentence saying
why, and the sentence is the argument you would have to beat. If the cell is
`▪`, the combination renders and there is a live row for it on
`/Specimen/States`. If the condition is not on the family's matrix at all, the
entry's _what its matrix does not ask_ names the hole.

## The contract - what a block may be, and may never be

These 7 laws hold before any family's own matrix is
read. They are the only prose in this document that is not derived: they are the
document's constitution (`DESIGN-COMPLETE.md` §4.2 and §4.4), restated as a
table because a contributor reads a table and skips a paragraph. A law with no
check is a preference, so each one names what a reviewer looks at.

| #   | LAW                                                      | MEANS                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | CHECK                                                                                                                                                                             | SOURCE |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| 01  | A BLOCK IS STRUCTURE, NOT A SURFACE                      | It lives inside a Jelly surface and never replaces one. A `RecordEntry` that needs a card sits inside a `jelly-card`, never inside a `&lt;div class="...-card"&gt;` painted by a partial.                                                            | Open the block's file: does it render a surface, or does it render structure on a surface the page supplies?                                                                      | §4.2   |
| 02  | A BLOCK RENDERS PROPS ONLY                               | No `&lt;script&gt;`, no `client:*`, no DOM access, no `any`. Interaction state is CSS, and the no-JavaScript fallback is the state itself.                                                                                                           | Search the file for `client:`, `&lt;script`, `document.` and `window.` - a block that has one is an island and belongs in `Component/` with a hydration directive the page chose. | §4.2   |
| 03  | A BLOCK NEVER DERIVES DATA IT WAS NOT GIVEN              | No sorting, no renumbering, no re-casing, no invented slash, no computed count. A count is composed from the rows the block holds, by `RegisterLine.ts`, and from nothing else.                                                                      | Does the block call `.sort(`, `.map((x, i) =&gt; i + 1)` or a template literal around a number? A count that is not `rows.length` is a figure with no source.                     | §4.2   |
| 04  | A BLOCK THAT NEEDS A SHAPE DECLARES IT AND REPORTS       | `Record/Type.ts` is the shared contract. A block that needs a shape it does not carry declares a local type and reports the mismatch, because an honest local shape beats a forced fit against a wrong shared one.                                   | Does the block cast a prop into a shared type, or declare what it actually takes?                                                                                                 | §4.2   |
| 05  | A CARD EXTENDS ADDITIVELY, AND NEVER CHANGES A SIGNATURE | A card adds a prop; it never changes one another file uses. A borrowed class is not a block - the hero's facts ledger and the specimen strip both carried `record-ledger` classes without importing `RecordLedger`, and that is why the two drifted. | `git diff` on the block's props: every line is an addition, or the change is reported before it lands.                                                                            | §4.2   |
| 06  | ONE COMPONENT, ONE PARTIAL, AND TOKENS ONLY              | `RecordBand.astro` owns `System/Record/_Band.scss`, wired once with `@use`. Colour, size and space come from `var(--...)`; a literal hex or px is a defect unless it is a hairline or `0`.                                                           | Grep the partial for `#[0-9a-f]` and `[0-9]px`: two hits and the component has left the theme.                                                                                    | §4.4   |
| 07  | NOTHING INSIDE A JELLY SURFACE IS A SECOND SURFACE       | A `Record*` block, a `bare` band, the page's `h1` in the opening artifact, a form, a ledger, a matrix, a well, a captioned figure - and never a second Jelly surface, a band that paints its own fill, or a Jelly element repainted by a lane class. | Is there a card inside the card, a border inside the border, or a Jelly element with a lane class on it? A card inside a card is never right.                                     | §4.3   |

## The spine - the 22 conditions every family is measured against

The families ask their own questions; the states gallery folds those question
sets onto one spine so that two families can be compared at all. This is that
spine, with the figure every component of the document contributes. `UNASKED`
is the third disposition: a condition no family's matrix has a column for, and
therefore a hole rather than a failure.

## The families

### `# 01` /THE FIELD

**For.** A control's states are the design: what it is when it is empty, when it is refused, when it is read-only, and when the reader cannot see it at all.

**Read for.** The input family's matrix and its live rows - the fields, the labels, the selects, the toggles and the one control that is a paragraph.

**Its boundary.** The input family asks what a control does when the world is unkind to the control itself - invalid, required, hint, counter, addon - and leaves the conditions that belong to the block holding it to that block. A field cannot fail a read it never makes, and its age is the record's as-of rather than the input's.

#### What it may never be

The strongest 4 of the 44 sentences this
family's matrix uses to mark a combination impossible. The numbering is the
family's, and the matrix below references it cell by cell.

1. **2 cells.** A label names one control; it has no set.

    `LABEL / ONE ITEM / LABEL / MANY ITEMS`

2. **1 cell.** An input holds one value. A set of one is a Select's or a radio group's subject, not an input's.

    `INPUT / ONE ITEM`

3. **1 cell.** An input has no members. The set it belongs to is the form's, and the form's row owns that column.

    `INPUT / MANY ITEMS`

4. **1 cell.** A prefix hangs in a first-line gutter, and a multi-line box has none: the prefix would sit beside the box, not inside it. The suffix is built - it is the counter.

    `TEXTAREA / ADDON`

#### The row that proves it

| MARK | STATE         | PART  |
| ---- | ------------- | ----- |
| `28` | NARROW COLUMN | Input |

**When it is right.** A 16rem column: the label wraps, the action stacks under the control, and the value still fits - the query is on the field.

**Why this row.** A field is a control in a container, and the container is the part a designer forgets: at 16rem the label wraps, the action stacks and the value still fits, because the query is on the field rather than on the page.

**See it.** `/Specimen/States` - the family's row on the states gallery; `/Specimen#field` - the family's own matrix.

Every sentence the matrix uses, numbered as the cells reference them:

**1.** 2 cells - A label names one control; it has no set. `LABEL / ONE ITEM / LABEL / MANY ITEMS`

**2.** 1 cell - An input holds one value. A set of one is a Select's or a radio group's subject, not an input's. `INPUT / ONE ITEM`

**3.** 1 cell - An input has no members. The set it belongs to is the form's, and the form's row owns that column. `INPUT / MANY ITEMS`

**4.** 1 cell - A prefix hangs in a first-line gutter, and a multi-line box has none: the prefix would sit beside the box, not inside it. The suffix is built - it is the counter. `TEXTAREA / ADDON`

**5.** 1 cell - A textarea holds one value, however many lines it takes. `TEXTAREA / ONE ITEM`

**6.** 1 cell - Its members are lines, and lines are not items a control selects between. `TEXTAREA / MANY ITEMS`

**7.** 1 cell - A label is not focusable. It carries the field's focus through `for`, and a ring of its own would be a second target for one field. `LABEL / FOCUS`

**8.** 1 cell - A label has no value to fill. `LABEL / FILLED`

**9.** 1 cell - A label is a word: it is present or it is absent. An empty label is a control with no name, which is a defect rather than a state. `LABEL / EMPTY`

**10.** 1 cell - A passed value is the control's fact. The label states what the field wants, never whether it got it. `LABEL / VALID`

**11.** 1 cell - An addon belongs to the control's box. A label has no box. `LABEL / ADDON`

**12.** 1 cell - A label is printed with the skeleton, not loaded by it - the schema is the one thing a loading field already knows. `LABEL / LOADING`

**13.** 1 cell - A label states what the field wants. What arrived is the control's sentence. `LABEL / PARTIAL`

**14.** 1 cell - HTML has no read-only checkbox. A value that must not change is `disabled` with the value printed beside it - a checkbox that looks pressable and is not is worse than one that says it cannot be pressed. `CHECKBOX / READ-ONLY`

**15.** 1 cell - Nothing to count. The selection count belongs to the group, and the group's row is `MANY ITEMS`. `CHECKBOX / COUNTER`

**16.** 1 cell - A checkbox has no box for an addon to sit in. `CHECKBOX / ADDON`

**17.** 1 cell - A checkbox is a boolean: it is known or it is not, and not-known is the skeleton. `CHECKBOX / PARTIAL`

**18.** 1 cell - A radio group that cannot change is `disabled`; a read-only radio is a mark that lies about being pressable. `RADIO GROUP / READ-ONLY`

**19.** 1 cell - A radio group selects one, so there is no selection to count. Its size is the option count, which is `MANY ITEMS`. `RADIO GROUP / COUNTER`

**20.** 1 cell - A group has no box; its frame is its legend. `RADIO GROUP / ADDON`

**21.** 1 cell - One of a set is either chosen or not. There is no half-chosen radio. `RADIO GROUP / PARTIAL`

**22.** 1 cell - A switch that cannot be flipped is disabled. A read-only switch would be a control that looks like it will answer and will not. `SWITCH / READ-ONLY`

**23.** 1 cell - A switch has a default, so it is never empty and never missing. A gate that must be on is a required checkbox, where the mark is the consent. `SWITCH / REQUIRED`

**24.** 1 cell - A boolean has nothing to count. `SWITCH / COUNTER`

**25.** 1 cell - A switch has no box for an addon to sit in. `SWITCH / ADDON`

**26.** 1 cell - A switch is one boolean; it has no set. `SWITCH / ONE ITEM`

**27.** 1 cell - A row of switches is a settings list - a `FieldSet` of switches, not one switch with members. `SWITCH / MANY ITEMS`

**28.** 1 cell - A switch reports a state it holds; a state it does not know yet is the skeleton. `SWITCH / PARTIAL`

**29.** 1 cell - A slider cannot be empty: it starts at its minimum, and a range with no value is not a range. `SLIDER / EMPTY`

**30.** 1 cell - The track enforces its own bounds, so a value outside them is impossible. A slider that must be above a floor states the floor in its hint, not in an error. `SLIDER / INVALID`

**31.** 1 cell - There is no invalid to be the opposite of, so a valid slider would be a green mark with nothing behind it. `SLIDER / VALID`

**32.** 1 cell - A slider is a control; one that cannot move is disabled. A value the reader may only read is printed, not slid. `SLIDER / READ-ONLY`

**33.** 1 cell - A slider always has a value, so it is never the thing a form is missing. `SLIDER / REQUIRED`

**34.** 1 cell - A slider is one value; it has no members. `SLIDER / ONE ITEM`

**35.** 1 cell - A range is continuous. A set of ranges is a matrix, not a slider. `SLIDER / MANY ITEMS`

**36.** 1 cell - A slider's value is always a number the reader chose; there is no half-known position. `SLIDER / PARTIAL`

**37.** 1 cell - A select has no read-only state. A value that must not change is printed as a value, not offered as a choice. `SELECT / READ-ONLY`

**38.** 1 cell - The trigger is already a frame with a `:` label and its disclosure mark. An addon would be a second frame inside the first. `SELECT / ADDON`

**39.** 1 cell - A code that must not change is disabled once accepted, and the acceptance is a sentence under it. `INPUT OTP / READ-ONLY`

**40.** 1 cell - The slots are the box. A prefix would be a seventh cell that is not part of the code. `INPUT OTP / ADDON`

**41.** 1 cell - A code's length is fixed by its slots, so there is no long text - an eight-character code is `MANY ITEMS`, not a long one. `INPUT OTP / LONG TEXT`

**42.** 1 cell - One slot is not a code; a code is a fixed set of slots. `INPUT OTP / ONE ITEM`

**43.** 1 cell - A form is open or it is closed. A form the reader may not change is a receipt, and the receipt is its own block. `FORM / READ-ONLY`

**44.** 1 cell - A form has no addon. The prefix of a form is its route, and the route is the page's, not the block's. `FORM / ADDON`

#### What the exploration changed

**◎ IMPROVEMENTS: UNAVAILABLE.** `CONTENT/SPECIMEN/FIELD.TS` carries no `Improvements` export: its family was printed before the convention existed, so the behaviours its matrix produced are recorded as the notes on the cells it built - and those notes are in the matrix above. The absence is stated rather than filled, because a behaviour with no cell behind it is a preference.

#### What its matrix does not ask

7 conditions, 70 cells unanswered - `ERROR`, `STALE`, `MISSING`, `DENIED`, `NO ACTION`, `ON PAPER`, `REDUCED`. The family's matrix has no column for these, and `/Specimen/States` §THE UNASKED prints the sentence that says why.

#### Its live rows

- **/THE CONDITIONS** - The fifteen conditions a field has to hold, in the order the state layer names them.
- **/THE CONTROLS** - The other nine parts of the family, each printed once at the state it is best known by.
- **/THE SKINS** - The same field in four boxes. A field that reads differently in a card is two components wearing one name.

### `# 02` /THE OVERLAY

**For.** An overlay is judged in the two seconds after a click: what it covers, what it returns to, and the five ways out.

**Read for.** The overlay family's matrix, its five-rule dismissal contract, and every state printed live - a slip, a drawer, a modal, a menu and a command well.

**Its boundary.** The overlay family asks what a panel does in the two seconds after a click - hover, focus, current, submenu, taller than the viewport, near the edge, trigger removed - and leaves the states of the content it covers to the block that renders it. A slip is dismissed; it is not edited, and it outlives no target.

#### What it may never be

The strongest 4 of the 27 sentences this
family's matrix uses to mark a combination impossible. The numbering is the
family's, and the matrix below references it cell by cell.

1. **6 cells.** a modal panel has no persistent row to mark. `current` is the item grammar's state - the value in force in a set the reader is choosing from - and a dialog, a sheet, a drawer or a popover holds no set it chooses from.

    `DIALOG / CURRENT / DRAWER / CURRENT / SHEET / CURRENT / POPOVER / CURRENT / HOVERCARD / CURRENT / ICONTOOLTIP / CURRENT`

2. **6 cells.** a panel takes its density from the block inside it - `RecordLedger`, the `.Slip__Row` grammar, a `RecordWell`. A second density switch on the panel would be a second source of truth for one rhythm, and the first thing it would do is disagree with the block. The slip's `data-density` is the _list_ surfaces' switch - it tightens a row, and a panel has no rows of its own to tighten.

    `DIALOG / DENSE / DRAWER / DENSE / SHEET / DENSE / POPOVER / DENSE / HOVERCARD / DENSE / ICONTOOLTIP / DENSE`

3. **6 cells.** a panel holds content, not menu rows. A submenu three deep is a menu's problem - the slip's own `Trail` head states the path - and a panel that grew one would be a menu in a box.

    `DIALOG / SUBMENU ×3 / DRAWER / SUBMENU ×3 / SHEET / SUBMENU ×3 / POPOVER / SUBMENU ×3 / HOVERCARD / SUBMENU ×3 / ICONTOOLTIP / SUBMENU ×3`

4. **4 cells.** a modal portals to the body. It cannot sit inside a card - and a panel painted inside a card would be a card inside a card, which is the one composition the identity refuses.

    `DIALOG / INSIDE A CARD / DRAWER / INSIDE A CARD / SHEET / INSIDE A CARD / COMMAND / INSIDE A CARD`

**Why this row.** A panel is judged by what it does when its content outgrows it: at sixty rows the head and the foot pin and only the body scrolls, so the reader never loses the way out.

Every sentence the matrix uses, numbered as the cells reference them:

**1.** 6 cells - a modal panel has no persistent row to mark. `current` is the item grammar's state - the value in force in a set the reader is choosing from - and a dialog, a sheet, a drawer or a popover holds no set it chooses from. `DIALOG / CURRENT / DRAWER / CURRENT / SHEET / CURRENT / POPOVER / CURRENT / HOVERCARD / CURRENT / ICONTOOLTIP / CURRENT`

**2.** 6 cells - a panel takes its density from the block inside it - `RecordLedger`, the `.Slip__Row` grammar, a `RecordWell`. A second density switch on the panel would be a second source of truth for one rhythm, and the first thing it would do is disagree with the block. The slip's `data-density` is the _list_ surfaces' switch - it tightens a row, and a panel has no rows of its own to tighten. `DIALOG / DENSE / DRAWER / DENSE / SHEET / DENSE / POPOVER / DENSE / HOVERCARD / DENSE / ICONTOOLTIP / DENSE`

**3.** 6 cells - a panel holds content, not menu rows. A submenu three deep is a menu's problem - the slip's own `Trail` head states the path - and a panel that grew one would be a menu in a box. `DIALOG / SUBMENU ×3 / DRAWER / SUBMENU ×3 / SHEET / SUBMENU ×3 / POPOVER / SUBMENU ×3 / HOVERCARD / SUBMENU ×3 / ICONTOOLTIP / SUBMENU ×3`

**4.** 4 cells - a modal portals to the body. It cannot sit inside a card - and a panel painted inside a card would be a card inside a card, which is the one composition the identity refuses. `DIALOG / INSIDE A CARD / DRAWER / INSIDE A CARD / SHEET / INSIDE A CARD / COMMAND / INSIDE A CARD`

**5.** 3 cells - a tooltip is a label the trigger already carries. There is nothing to arrive and nothing to fail: the announcement exists before the hover does. `ICONTOOLTIP / LOADING / ICONTOOLTIP / ERROR / ICONTOOLTIP / PARTIAL`

**6.** 3 cells - a menu is composed with the region or the trigger that opens it: its rows exist before the gesture does. A menu whose rows had to arrive would be a menu opened before its subject existed, and the family's loading arm belongs to the slips that fetch - the palette, a dialog, a popover. `CONTEXTMENU / LOADING / DROPDOWNMENU / LOADING / MENUBAR / LOADING`

**7.** 3 cells - an action's failure belongs to the surface it acted on, not to the menu that closed on selection. The menu is gone before the request is sent, so an error body inside it would be a body nobody sees. `CONTEXTMENU / ERROR / DROPDOWNMENU / ERROR / MENUBAR / ERROR`

**8.** 3 cells - a menu is either composed or it is not. A row whose value has not arrived prints `◎ UNAVAILABLE` in its own meta cell - the honest per-row answer - rather than the whole slip declaring itself partial. `CONTEXTMENU / PARTIAL / DROPDOWNMENU / PARTIAL / MENUBAR / PARTIAL`

**9.** 2 cells - a hover card's content is the caller's children, rendered with the trigger. There is no register to arrive, so there is no loading arm - and inventing one would make a gloss wait. `HOVERCARD / LOADING / HOVERCARD / PARTIAL`

**10.** 2 cells - a hover card is dismissed by the pointer leaving the trigger. A trigger removed while the card is open has already been un-hovered, so the pointer's own exit is the rule - a second guard would close a card that is already closing. `HOVERCARD / TRIGGER REMOVED / ICONTOOLTIP / TRIGGER REMOVED`

**11.** 2 cells - the palette's index is static and cannot fail. Its adverse state is `◎ NO RECORD` and the rail's handoff row, not an error body - and the `SlipError` arm belongs to the panels that run an action. `COMMAND / ERROR / COMMAND / PARTIAL`

**12.** 1 cell - a modal is centred by definition. It has no anchor to collide with, so there is no edge for it to be near. `DIALOG / NEAR THE RIGHT EDGE`

**13.** 1 cell - a drawer is anchored to an edge, so _near the edge_ is its resting position rather than a collision it has to survive. `DRAWER / NEAR THE RIGHT EDGE`

**14.** 1 cell - a sheet is anchored to an edge, so _near the edge_ is its resting position rather than a collision it has to survive. `SHEET / NEAR THE RIGHT EDGE`

**15.** 1 cell - a popover caps at 24rem and scrolls inside that cap. It is anchored to a trigger that is on screen, so it can never be taller than the viewport - the cap is what makes the question unaskable. `POPOVER / TALLER THAN THE VIEWPORT`

**16.** 1 cell - a popover is a gloss on one control. At the band's width it would be a sheet, and the arrival from a 2px side offset would be a lie about where it came from. `POPOVER / WIDE BAND`

**17.** 1 cell - a hover card has no disabled state. Its trigger is a reference - a name, a glyph, a term - and a reference that cannot be hovered is text, not a control. `HOVERCARD / DISABLED`

**18.** 1 cell - a hover card's content is the caller's children. There is no register to be empty: a card with nothing in it is a caller bug, and the component does not invent an arm for it. `HOVERCARD / EMPTY`

**19.** 1 cell - a hover card states what a thing is, not what an action did. It runs nothing, so it has nothing to fail at. `HOVERCARD / ERROR`

**20.** 1 cell - a hover card is a gloss. At the band's width it would be a popover that never admitted it, and the reader would lose the pointer path back to the trigger. `HOVERCARD / WIDE BAND`

**21.** 1 cell - a tooltip's trigger is not a control, so it cannot be disabled. Its glyph can be _unavailable_, and that is a different statement - the `◎` the cap prints before the label. `ICONTOOLTIP / DISABLED`

**22.** 1 cell - a tooltip with no label is not rendered at all - `IconTooltip` returns null, because an unlabelled icon is a decoration rather than a control. An empty arm here would be an arm for a state the component refuses to enter. `ICONTOOLTIP / EMPTY`

**23.** 1 cell - a tooltip is a gloss on one control. At the band's width it would stop being a gloss; the detail arm caps at 22rem for exactly that reason. `ICONTOOLTIP / WIDE BAND`

**24.** 1 cell - a context menu is sized by its longest row, at the pointer. At the band's width it would be a panel anchored to a click. `CONTEXTMENU / WIDE BAND`

**25.** 1 cell - a dropdown is sized by its longest row, under its trigger. At the band's width it would be a panel rather than a menu. `DROPDOWNMENU / WIDE BAND`

**26.** 1 cell - a command list is flat by design: cmdk's model is one listbox with one selection, and the foot states `↑↓ MOVE` over that one list. A nested listbox inside it would break the arrow keys the foot promises. `COMMAND / SUBMENU ×3`

**27.** 1 cell - the palette is centred in the viewport at `12vh`. It has no anchor, so it has no edge to collide with. `COMMAND / NEAR THE RIGHT EDGE`

#### What the exploration changed

**◎ IMPROVEMENTS: UNAVAILABLE.** `CONTENT/SPECIMEN/OVERLAY.TS` carries no `Improvements` export: its family was printed before the convention existed, so the behaviours its matrix produced are recorded as the notes on the cells it built - and those notes are in the matrix above. The absence is stated rather than filled, because a behaviour with no cell behind it is a preference.

#### What its matrix does not ask

9 conditions, 90 cells unanswered - `STALE`, `READ-ONLY`, `MISSING`, `DENIED`, `IN A BAND`, `WITH ACTION`, `NO ACTION`, `ON PAPER`, `REDUCED`. The family's matrix has no column for these, and `/Specimen/States` §THE UNASKED prints the sentence that says why.

#### Its live rows

- **/THE PANELS** - The four surfaces that take the reader's whole attention: a dialog, a drawer, a sheet, a popover. Each one is a slip with a head, a body and a foot - and each one is printed here in the four states it was never printed in: loading, empty, failed, and outgrown.
- **/THE CARDS AND THE CAP** - The three small surfaces: a hover card, a tooltip's cap and a tooltip's detail arm. The rule they print is the family's size rule - a cap for a mark, a slip for a document - and the two arms are shown side by side so the difference is a size, not a mood.
- **/THE MENUS** - The four list surfaces: a context menu, a dropdown, a menubar and the command palette. They are one instrument: the same register line, the same `[mark] [label] [meta]` row, the same five states, the same foot. A submenu states its depth as a path, and a menu with no rows says so rather than opening blank.

### `# 03` /THE DISPLAY

**For.** A display is read rather than used: its worst state is not a failed action but a figure that lies about its own extent.

**Read for.** The display family's matrix, its verdict on the two components no page mounts, and every state a chart, a calendar, a table or a figure is read in.

**Its boundary.** The display family asks the widest question set of the ten and still leaves one condition out: a display is read, so `read-only` names nothing it could be refused. It also never asks for a missing target or a denied reader, because a figure has no door and no owner.

    `BADGE / ERROR`

    `BADGE / WIDE`

Every sentence the matrix uses, numbered as the cells reference them:

**1.** 1 cell - A badge is not a control, so it cannot be disabled. A claim that is no longer current prints in the quiet ink, which is a state of the claim and not of the reader's permission. `BADGE / DISABLED`

**2.** 1 cell - A badge with no text is a coloured rectangle. An empty badge states nothing, so it is not printed at all - the set that would have held it prints its own absence instead. `BADGE / EMPTY`

**3.** 1 cell - A badge carries no action, so it cannot fail. The refusal belongs to the control beside it, and that control is where the STATUS word goes. `BADGE / ERROR`

**4.** 1 cell - A badge takes its content's width. A badge at full band width would be a status bar, and the site has one of those in the header. `BADGE / WIDE`

**5.** 1 cell - A badge's only interval is a colour wash on hover, and colour is not motion. There is nothing to remove. `BADGE / REDUCED MOTION`

**6.** 1 cell - A card inside a card is the one composition the identity forbids (§1.3). The card is the artifact's surface - one artifact, one card - so there is no second card to nest. `CARD / IN A CARD`

**7.** 1 cell - The table's only interval is the row's hover wash and the head's pin, and neither is motion. A disclosure inside a cell owns its own reduced-motion path. `TABLE / REDUCED MOTION`

**8.** 1 cell - One tab is not a choice. A single view prints its title, not a tab strip - a strip of one is a control that answers only itself. `TABS / ONE ITEM`

**9.** 1 cell - A tab strip takes the width of its labels. Stretched across a band it would read as a nav, and the header already is one. `TABS / WIDE`

**10.** 1 cell - A tab strip has no interval: the panel swap is a state change, and the reveal on focus is `nearest`, which does not animate. `TABS / REDUCED MOTION`

**11.** 1 cell - An accordion has no selected item. Open is not selected: `aria-expanded` is the state, and a stack that also carried a selection would have two states for one region. `ACCORDION / ACTIVE`

**12.** 1 cell - A collapsible has no selected item: the region is open or closed, and `aria-expanded` is the whole of its state. `COLLAPSIBLE / ACTIVE`

**13.** 1 cell - A collapsible holds one region. Many regions are an accordion, and the family keeps the two apart on purpose - a component that did both would be one component pretending to be two. `COLLAPSIBLE / MANY ITEMS`

**14.** 1 cell - A progress bar is not focusable. The job it reports owns the focus, and the bar is a figure. `PROGRESS / FOCUS`

**15.** 1 cell - A job cannot be disabled; it can be paused, which is a state of the job rather than of the reader's permission. `PROGRESS / DISABLED`

**16.** 1 cell - An empty progress is a track at zero, which is the rest cell. There is no third thing between nothing and a figure. `PROGRESS / EMPTY`

**17.** 1 cell - One step is a completion, not a measurement: it prints `COMPLETE`, not a bar of one. `PROGRESS / ONE ITEM`

**18.** 1 cell - A skeleton has one state - waiting. At rest it would be an empty shape, which is a decorative box. `SKELETON / REST`

**19.** 1 cell - A skeleton is not focusable. The thing it stands in for will be. `SKELETON / FOCUS`

**20.** 1 cell - A skeleton has no chosen state: it is replaced, not selected. `SKELETON / ACTIVE`

**21.** 1 cell - Nothing can be disabled before it exists. `SKELETON / DISABLED`

**22.** 1 cell - A skeleton for an empty set is a lie. If the answer is nothing, the empty state prints, not a placeholder. `SKELETON / EMPTY`

**23.** 1 cell - A failed load stops being a skeleton: the error state takes its place and the skeleton is unmounted. `SKELETON / ERROR`

**24.** 1 cell - A skeleton has no as-of. It is the absence of a value, not an old one. `SKELETON / STALE`

**25.** 1 cell - A skeleton is never printed. Paper has no waiting. `SKELETON / PRINT`

**26.** 1 cell - A rule is not focusable. `SEPARATOR / FOCUS`

**27.** 1 cell - A rule separates; it is not chosen. `SEPARATOR / ACTIVE`

**28.** 1 cell - A rule cannot be disabled. A rule that is not wanted is not printed. `SEPARATOR / DISABLED`

**29.** 1 cell - A rule has nothing to wait for. `SEPARATOR / LOADING`

**30.** 1 cell - A separator with nothing on either side separates nothing; the space is the separator there. `SEPARATOR / EMPTY`

**31.** 1 cell - A rule states no facts, so it cannot state an unknown one. `SEPARATOR / PARTIAL`

**32.** 1 cell - A rule cannot fail. `SEPARATOR / ERROR`

**33.** 1 cell - A rule has no as-of. `SEPARATOR / STALE`

**34.** 1 cell - A rule between one thing and itself is a box. `SEPARATOR / ONE ITEM`

**35.** 1 cell - A rule carries no action. The control that clears a filter is a button, not a separator. `SEPARATOR / WITH ACTION`

**36.** 1 cell - A rule has no interval. `SEPARATOR / REDUCED MOTION`

**37.** 1 cell - An avatar is not chosen; the record it names is. `AVATAR / ACTIVE`

**38.** 1 cell - An identity cannot be disabled. A record can be archived, and the avatar prints the tombstone: the mark stays and the ink goes. `AVATAR / DISABLED`

**39.** 1 cell - An avatar with no identity is a blank square. The `◎` fallback is the honest form, and it is the partial cell. `AVATAR / EMPTY`

**40.** 1 cell - An avatar is one identity by definition. A set of identities is `AvatarGroup`. `AVATAR / ONE ITEM`

**41.** 1 cell - An avatar has no interval. `AVATAR / REDUCED MOTION`

**42.** 1 cell - An alert has no chosen state. It is read, and dismissed. `ALERT / ACTIVE`

**43.** 1 cell - An alert cannot be disabled. A reader who may not act sees the `denied` composition, which is a state of the surface and not of the alert. `ALERT / DISABLED`

**44.** 1 cell - An alert with nothing in it is a rule. An empty alert states nothing, so it is not printed. `ALERT / EMPTY`

**45.** 1 cell - A crumb is a place, not a control. A place that cannot be reached is a tombstone, which the missing state prints. `BREADCRUMB / DISABLED`

**46.** 1 cell - A trail of no crumbs is not a trail. A page with no parent prints its index instead. `BREADCRUMB / EMPTY`

**47.** 1 cell - A trail is structural: it is where the page is, not what it knows, so it has no as-of. `BREADCRUMB / STALE`

**48.** 1 cell - The trail does not move. `BREADCRUMB / REDUCED MOTION`

**49.** 1 cell - A page number is not a fact that ages. `PAGINATION / STALE`

**50.** 1 cell - A pagination control prints links to pages that are not printed. The printed sheet prints all its rows. `PAGINATION / PRINT`

**51.** 1 cell - A page change is a navigation, not an interval. `PAGINATION / REDUCED MOTION`

**52.** 1 cell - A viewport is not chosen. `SCROLLAREA / ACTIVE`

**53.** 1 cell - A viewport cannot be disabled. A frame that must not scroll is not a scroll area - it is a frame. `SCROLLAREA / DISABLED`

**54.** 1 cell - One row does not scroll. A scroll area around one row is a box with a bar that can never move. `SCROLLAREA / ONE ITEM`

**55.** 1 cell - A scroll is the reader's own gesture; there is no interval to remove. `SCROLLAREA / REDUCED MOTION`

**56.** 1 cell - Panes are frames; they do not wait. What waits is the content inside one, and that is the skeleton's cell. `RESIZABLE / LOADING`

**57.** 1 cell - One pane is not a seam. A single pane is a frame. `RESIZABLE / ONE ITEM`

**58.** 1 cell - A carousel on paper hides every slide but one. The sheet prints the set as a matrix or a plate instead. `CAROUSEL / PRINT`

**59.** 1 cell - A figure is not a control. There is nothing to disable; a series that cannot be read prints `UNAVAILABLE`. `CHART / DISABLED`

**60.** 1 cell - One bar is a number, not a figure. The ledger prints it, at the register, without an axis. `CHART / ONE ITEM`

**61.** 1 cell - A day cell holds a number and a mark. A long label belongs beside the month, not inside a day. `CALENDAR / LONG TEXT`

**62.** 1 cell - A calendar is a month. A set of one day is a date, and a date prints as a register line. `CALENDAR / ONE ITEM`

**63.** 1 cell - A month does not move; a month change is a new plate. `CALENDAR / REDUCED MOTION`

**64.** 1 cell - A receipt is not chosen; it is read or dismissed. `SONNER / ACTIVE`

**65.** 1 cell - A receipt cannot be disabled. The action it reports can be, and the receipt says so. `SONNER / DISABLED`

**66.** 1 cell - An empty receipt is a frame with no sentence. A receipt states an action or it is not printed. `SONNER / EMPTY`

**67.** 1 cell - A receipt is a slip at the corner. Stretched across a band it would be an alert, and the alert is the component for that. `SONNER / WIDE`

**68.** 1 cell - A receipt is the four seconds after an action. Paper has no four seconds. `SONNER / PRINT`

#### What the exploration changed

**◎ IMPROVEMENTS: UNAVAILABLE.** `CONTENT/SPECIMEN/DISPLAY.TS` carries no `Improvements` export: its family was printed before the convention existed, so the behaviours its matrix produced are recorded as the notes on the cells it built - and those notes are in the matrix above. The absence is stated rather than filled, because a behaviour with no cell behind it is a preference.

#### What its matrix does not ask

3 conditions, 57 cells unanswered - `READ-ONLY`, `MISSING`, `DENIED`. The family's matrix has no column for these, and `/Specimen/States` §THE UNASKED prints the sentence that says why.

#### Its live rows

- **/WHAT THE DOCUMENT READS WITH** - The instruments the page carries its facts in: a table read across, a card that is one artifact, and the marks that name a claim. Every row here is a state of the same three parts, because the reading instruments are the ones whose adverse states nobody notices are missing.
- **/HOW IT DISCLOSES** - Four parts, two grammars: a strip of sibling views and a stack of closed sections. The states are the ones that only appear when the labels are too long, the set is empty, or the reader asked for less motion - and all three are printed here rather than assumed.
- **/HOW IT MEASURES** - A job's progress, a record that has not arrived, a figure that argues, and a month. The two components the document does not mount are here, with the verdict on whether they should exist at all - printed rather than filed away.
- **/WHAT IT SAYS QUIETLY** - The parts that carry a page without being read: the rule that names its seam, the seal that stands for a person, the alert that states a failure, the trail, the page control, the frame, the seam, the position, and the receipt. A family is judged by these, because they are the ones a reader never notices working.

### `# 04` /THE RECORD

**For.** A ledger is believed, not used. A fact that has lost its adverse state is a fact that lies, and a lie is the one defect this family cannot survive.

**Read for.** The ledger, the matrix, the stage, the well, the figure, the pair, the archive and the register - every form the document states a fact in.

**Its boundary.** The ledger family asks its long values as two arms - `LONG KEY` and `LONG VALUE` - which is the most precise answer on this page and the reason one cell here is read from two columns. It leaves the two arms no matrix asks, because a ledger is believed: it has no action to deny and no target to lose.

#### What it may never be

The strongest 4 of the 72 sentences this
family's matrix uses to mark a combination impossible. The numbering is the
family's, and the matrix below references it cell by cell.

1. **1 cell.** A ledger prints facts, and a failed action is not a fact about an object. Its cause, its next step and its retry are `RecordFailure`'s three fields; a ledger that grew them would be a condition block wearing a list's grammar.

    `LEDGER / ERROR`

2. **1 cell.** A ledger is not a control, so it cannot be disabled. A fact the reader may not see is a fact the page does not print, and that is a permission decision above the block - the block has nothing to withhold.

    `LEDGER / DISABLED`

3. **1 cell.** A ledger is read-only by construction: it is a `&lt;dl&gt;`, it ships no script and it holds no input. There is no editable arm for read-only to be the absence of.

    `LEDGER / READ-ONLY`

4. **1 cell.** A ledger has no action slot. The action belongs beside it in the artifact that holds it, which is where the tier's one `.emphasis-expressive` control goes - one action per artifact, never one per fact.

    `LEDGER / WITH ACTION`

#### The row that proves it

| MARK | STATE | PART   |

| `07` | STALE | Ledger |

**When it is right.** A fact older than the page: the value stays visible and `AS OF:` states its age beside it.

**Why this row.** A ledger is believed, and a fact older than its as-of is the one way a true fact becomes a false claim: the value stays visible and the age prints beside it.

**See it.** `/Specimen/States` - the family's row on the states gallery; `/Specimen#record` - the family's own matrix.

Every sentence the matrix uses, numbered as the cells reference them:

**1.** 1 cell - A ledger prints facts, and a failed action is not a fact about an object. Its cause, its next step and its retry are `RecordFailure`'s three fields; a ledger that grew them would be a condition block wearing a list's grammar. `LEDGER / ERROR`

**2.** 1 cell - A ledger is not a control, so it cannot be disabled. A fact the reader may not see is a fact the page does not print, and that is a permission decision above the block - the block has nothing to withhold. `LEDGER / DISABLED`

**3.** 1 cell - A ledger is read-only by construction: it is a `&lt;dl&gt;`, it ships no script and it holds no input. There is no editable arm for read-only to be the absence of. `LEDGER / READ-ONLY`

**4.** 1 cell - A ledger has no action slot. The action belongs beside it in the artifact that holds it, which is where the tier's one `.emphasis-expressive` control goes - one action per artifact, never one per fact. `LEDGER / WITH ACTION`

**5.** 1 cell - The ledger's only interval is the `&lt;details&gt;` a row opens with, and the browser opens that with no animation at all. There is nothing to remove for a reader who asked for less. `LEDGER / REDUCED MOTION`

**6.** 1 cell - A comparison states what each column is. A read that failed is a state word in the cell that failed - `UNAVAILABLE` in the vocabulary's tone - and a matrix-level error would be a second vocabulary for the same fact. `MATRIX / ERROR`

**7.** 1 cell - A matrix cell is a value without an age; the table's provenance is its caption, which is the block's one sentence about the whole comparison. An as-of per cell would be a fourth field in a three-field artifact. `MATRIX / STALE`

**8.** 1 cell - A matrix is not a control. There is no cell to disable, and a greyed-out comparison is a comparison nobody can read. `MATRIX / DISABLED`

**9.** 1 cell - A matrix is a printed table with no input and no script; read-only is not an absence it can have. `MATRIX / READ-ONLY`

**10.** 1 cell - A matrix row is not selectable: a comparison marks a CELL, and a selection would need a script the block does not ship. A set that needs a chosen row is a ledger with `selected`. `MATRIX / SELECTED`

**11.** 1 cell - A matrix row that opened would put a second artifact inside a cell, which §4.2 forbids. The detail a row discloses belongs in a ledger under the matrix, where a row may open. `MATRIX / ROW THAT OPENS`

**12.** 1 cell - A rail is a reading of positions, not an action. What fails on an axis is the link a stop points at, and a dead link is the browser's own statement. `COMPARE / ERROR`

**13.** 1 cell - A stop's position is a fact about an order, not a measurement: it has no as-of. A rail whose positions are out of date is a rail whose caption says so. `COMPARE / STALE`

**14.** 1 cell - A rail has no control to disable. An unreachable position is the `state` arm - a hollow tick and the vocabulary's word - which is a fact about the position and not about the reader's permission. `COMPARE / DISABLED`

**15.** 1 cell - The rail is printed: no input, no script, nothing to withhold. `COMPARE / READ-ONLY`

**16.** 1 cell - A rail marks which positions are reached with the stop's own state. A selection would be a choice among positions, and an axis is one order rather than a menu. `COMPARE / SELECTED`

**17.** 1 cell - A rail with more than six stops is a matrix. The block refuses to compress - a compressed rail is a table with the ends filed off - so a set of twenty positions is `RecordMatrix`'s work. `COMPARE / MANY ITEMS`

**18.** 1 cell - Documented refusal, not an omission: a rail has one rhythm at every length, and the block that needs tighter is the matrix. `COMPARE / DENSE`

**19.** 1 cell - A rail has no total: its two ends are the axis's own, and a sum of positions is not a position on an axis. `COMPARE / TOTAL ROW`

**20.** 1 cell - A stop is a position with one value, not a row with more of itself. A stop that opened would be a stage - and a stage is a different artifact. `COMPARE / ROW THAT OPENS`

**21.** 1 cell - A stop's value IS the action when it is a link. A button beside the rail would be a second order on one line, which is the thing the axis exists to prevent. `COMPARE / WITH ACTION`

**22.** 1 cell - A trace step is a path or it is not a step. A trace whose source names a file the tree does not carry prints the path and lets the link fail - which is the honest reading, and better than a step that says it is half there. `TRACE / PARTIAL`

**23.** 1 cell - A trace has no failed arm: what fails is the link, and a trace whose source could not be read has no steps at all - which is `empty`, with the source still printed under it. `TRACE / ERROR`

**24.** 1 cell - A trace is a reading taken at build time and its `SOURCE:` is that reading's provenance. An as-of on a path would date a file, and the file dates itself. `TRACE / STALE`

**25.** 1 cell - Nothing in a trace is a control: the index is a number, the arrow is a mark, and the path is a link or it is text. `TRACE / DISABLED`

**26.** 1 cell - The trace is printed and ships no script; there is no editable arm. `TRACE / READ-ONLY`

**27.** 1 cell - A trace is an order, not a set with a chosen member. The reader's place in it is the browser's scroll position, which is not the block's state. `TRACE / SELECTED`

**28.** 1 cell - Documented refusal: a trace compressed is a list of links, and a list of links is not evidence. `TRACE / DENSE`

**29.** 1 cell - A trace has no total. Its count is in the marker (`06 STEPS`) and it is the steps' own length, so a total row would count the same set twice. `TRACE / TOTAL ROW`

**30.** 1 cell - A step is one path and the one thing it carries. A step that opened would hold a second note, and the trace's note column is already the place for the second line. `TRACE / ROW THAT OPENS`

**31.** 1 cell - The path is the action when it leads somewhere. A trace with a button beside it would be a command list, which is `RecordWell`'s job. `TRACE / WITH ACTION`

**32.** 1 cell - A figure that could not be measured prints `UNAVAILABLE` in its own cell, in the vocabulary's ink - the block's state arm. A second, panel-level error shape would be two ways to say one thing. `INSTRUMENT / ERROR`

**33.** 1 cell - A panel of printed figures has no control. A figure that is not being updated is a figure with an `AS OF:`. `INSTRUMENT / DISABLED`

**34.** 1 cell - The panel is printed and ships no script; there is no editable arm. `INSTRUMENT / READ-ONLY`

**35.** 1 cell - A measure is a figure, not a choice. The panel's emphasis is `lead` - one figure set larger - and that is a rank, not a selection. `INSTRUMENT / SELECTED`

**36.** 1 cell - Documented refusal: an instrument is already the densest reading of a figure - four fields in one cell. A block that needs tighter needs fewer measures. `INSTRUMENT / DENSE`

**37.** 1 cell - A measure is four fields in one cell. A disclosure inside it would be a fifth field, and the block's contract says the panel holds nothing. `INSTRUMENT / ROW THAT OPENS`

**38.** 1 cell - A panel has no action slot. A figure that can be refreshed is a figure whose refresh belongs to the page, not to the number. `INSTRUMENT / WITH ACTION`

**39.** 1 cell - A plate-set's absent cell is a tombstone with a reason (`state` + `note`), which is the honest reading of a capture that is not there. An error arm would be a second word for the same absence. `PLATE SET / ERROR`

**40.** 1 cell - A plate's age is its manifest's, and the set prints one `SOURCE:` for the field. An as-of per cell would put a date under fifteen pictures that share one capture date. `PLATE SET / STALE`

**41.** 1 cell - Nothing in a plate-set is disabled. A cell that cannot be shown prints its state and its reason; a greyed-out frame would be a hole with a caption. `PLATE SET / DISABLED`

**42.** 1 cell - The set is printed and ships no script; there is no editable arm. `PLATE SET / READ-ONLY`

**43.** 1 cell - A field of figures is scanned, not chosen. A selected cell would need a script, and the set's own selection is the reader's eye. `PLATE SET / SELECTED`

**44.** 1 cell - Documented refusal: a set of figures is scanned at one size, and a denser set is a smaller claim about each picture. `PLATE SET / DENSE`

**45.** 1 cell - A set has no total row: its count is its register line (`PLATES␁15`), and a sum of pictures is not a picture. `PLATE SET / TOTAL ROW`

**46.** 1 cell - A cell does not disclose. Its frame is a door when the cell names a target (`href`) and a picture when it does not - a disclosure inside a figure would be a caption channel, which is `RecordPlate`'s job. `PLATE SET / ROW THAT OPENS`

**47.** 1 cell - A register states a count, and a count that did not arrive is `UNAVAILABLE` - the partial arm. There is no error arm because the line has no action that could fail. `REGISTER / ERROR`

**48.** 1 cell - A register has no age: it counts the rows under it, and if those rows are stale their own `AS OF:` says so. A register that dated itself would be a second provenance beside the block's. `REGISTER / STALE`

**49.** 1 cell - The line is not a control. It is the smallest complete statement the grammar has, and there is nothing on it to withhold. `REGISTER / DISABLED`

**50.** 1 cell - The register is printed and ships no script; there is no editable arm. `REGISTER / READ-ONLY`

**51.** 1 cell - A register names a set and counts it. There is no member to select, and a selected register would be a tab. `REGISTER / SELECTED`

**52.** 1 cell - A register's second half is a count: a figure or one word. There is no long-value arm, and a count that needed three lines would be a sentence, not a register. `REGISTER / LONG VALUE`

**53.** 1 cell - A register line has one size. It is the smallest complete statement the grammar has, and there is no smaller step above the 13px floor. `REGISTER / DENSE`

**54.** 1 cell - A register IS the total: `# WHAT CHANGES / 08` is the count of the set. A total row under a total line would count the same thing twice. `REGISTER / TOTAL ROW`

**55.** 1 cell - A register line opens nothing. It is the block's own name and extent, and what the block holds is printed under it. `REGISTER / ROW THAT OPENS`

**56.** 1 cell - The line carries no action. A register that could be pressed would be a disclosure, and a disclosure has a fold. `REGISTER / WITH ACTION`

**57.** 1 cell - The module composes a line; it performs no action, so it has nothing that can fail. A failed read is a count the caller cannot know, which is `RegisterUnavailable`. `REGISTER LINE / ERROR`

**58.** 1 cell - The shape carries a label and a count. An age is not part of a register - it is a fact about the rows, and the rows carry it. `REGISTER LINE / STALE`

**59.** 1 cell - `RegisterLine` is a data module: it composes no markup and holds no control, so there is nothing to disable. `REGISTER LINE / DISABLED`

**60.** 1 cell - Every register is read-only: the shape has no setter and the renderer prints it. There is no editable arm to be the absence of. `REGISTER LINE / READ-ONLY`

**61.** 1 cell - A register names one set. There is no second member for a selection to choose between. `REGISTER LINE / SELECTED`

**62.** 1 cell - The module trims a label and never measures it. A long label is the RENDERER's arm, which is why REGISTER / LONG KEY is built and this row's is not. `REGISTER LINE / LONG KEY`

**63.** 1 cell - A count is a figure or one word by construction: `Padded` pads, `RegisterUnavailable` prints `UNAVAILABLE`, and `RegisterWindow` joins two counts with `OF`. `REGISTER LINE / LONG VALUE`

**64.** 1 cell - A data module has no rhythm to tighten. Density is a rendering decision and belongs to the block that prints the line. `REGISTER LINE / DENSE`

**65.** 1 cell - The module has no width: it composes a string, and the string wraps or does not in the renderer's box. `REGISTER LINE / NARROW`

**66.** 1 cell - The module has no width for the same reason. `RegisterText` composes one line for a title or an `aria-label`; how wide it prints is the renderer's. `REGISTER LINE / WIDE`

**67.** 1 cell - The line is already the total. There is no second rank of count in the shape, and adding one would be a second register grammar. `REGISTER LINE / TOTAL ROW`

**68.** 1 cell - The shape has four fields and no body: there is nothing under a register to open. `REGISTER LINE / ROW THAT OPENS`

**69.** 1 cell - A module composes no markup, so it cannot be inside a card. The line REGISTER prints is the part that sits in one. `REGISTER LINE / IN A CARD`

**70.** 1 cell - A module composes no markup, so it cannot sit on a band either - the same answer as IN A CARD, and it is the answer for both because the question is about a surface and this row has none. `REGISTER LINE / IN A BAND`

**71.** 1 cell - The shape has no slot for a control. `REGISTER LINE / WITH ACTION`

**72.** 1 cell - The module has no interval. Motion is a rendering decision and this row renders nothing. `REGISTER LINE / REDUCED MOTION`

#### What the exploration changed

1. **LEDGER** - from `ROW THAT OPENS`

    **Found.** A build's three flags were three rows of the same rank as its target and its licence, so a ledger of six facts read as a ledger of nine. The detail existed; it had no rank.

    **Built.** `LedgerRow.open` prints the row as a `&lt;details&gt;` whose summary is the value, with the disclosed facts as the same row grammar one level in - and through `LedgerValue`, the renderer the row's own value uses, so a link, a literal or a state word cannot print two ways on either level. No script: the browser's disclosure is the behaviour and the mark layer's fold is its sign.

2. **LEDGER** - from `SELECTED`

    **Found.** A ledger that stated a default (`DEFAULT:`, `ACTIVE:`) printed it in the same ink as the other rows, so the one fact a reader needed to find was the one fact the eye had to hunt for.

    **Built.** `LedgerRow.selected` prints `aria-current` plus the attested square and a leading rule at the divider's ink. The accent stays out of it: a fact is not an action.

3. **LEDGER** - from `TOTAL ROW`

    **Found.** A set's sum was printed as one more row, so the reader could not tell a fact from the figure the facts add up to.

    **Built.** `LedgerRow.total` prints under the divider's rule with its value at the sub role and spans the grid, so a total in a two-column register is the total of the whole register and not of one half.

4. **LEDGER** - from `PARTIAL / STALE`

    **Found.** An unknown fact and a fact older than the page were both written as prose in the value column (`not yet measured`, `as of 14 Nov`), so the vocabulary's own words were the one place they were not used.

    **Built.** `LedgerRow.state` tints and marks a value that is a state word - the mark layer's hollow square, the vocabulary's ink - and `LedgerRow.asOf` prints `AS OF:` in the note channel. The word stays the caller's: the block tints, it never re-cases.

5. **MATRIX** - from `EMPTY`

    **Found.** A matrix with no rows printed its head over a blank body. It was the one block on the site that could print a comparison whose answer looked like nothing at all.

    **Built.** `state="empty"` keeps the head - the schema is still true when the values are not - and prints one cell spanning the table with the composed sentence.

6. **MATRIX** - from `LOADING`

    **Found.** There was no loading arm at all: a comparison whose values had not arrived printed an empty table, which reads as a comparison of nothing.

    **Built.** `state="loading"` prints three skeleton rows with a bar in every cell, and the head stays. The bar is the ledger's own, so the site has one way of drawing a value that has not arrived.

7. **MATRIX** - from `PARTIAL`

    **Found.** `UNAVAILABLE` in a cell read as a value that happened to be a word - the same ink and the same weight as `YES` - so the one honest answer in a compatibility table was the least visible.

    **Built.** A cell whose value is one of the eight state words takes the vocabulary's ink and the mark layer's square. `yes` and `no` keep their verdict marks: an answer that was not given is not a third answer.

8. **TRACE** - from `LOADING`

    **Found.** The type contract promised a skeleton and the block printed nothing: `state="loading"` changed the marker to `LOADING` and left the body empty, so a trace being read looked exactly like a trace that had failed.

    **Built.** Three steps with the index in ink and a bar where the path and the note will be. The index prints because the steps' order is the schema.

9. **TRACE** - from `EMPTY`

    **Found.** The block checked a state its type could not express (`empty`), and a caller that passed no sentence got a marker over nothing - a hole where a provenance statement belongs.

    **Built.** `Trace.state` now carries `empty`, and the block composes the sentence when the caller does not: the marker and the `SOURCE:` both survive, because a trace with nothing in it is still a claim about where the claim can be checked.

10. **COMPARE** - from `TWO SIDES EQUAL`

**Found.** Two positions carrying the same value printed as two ordinary ticks, so a tie looked exactly like a gap. The caption had to say what the rail could have shown.

**Built.** `CompareStop.equal` draws the interval between the two ticks in the rail's own ink: two positions at the same place read as one plateau, and the caption then explains it rather than announcing it.

11. **INSTRUMENT** - from `MISSING READING / LOADING`

**Found.** A panel whose figures had not arrived printed its caption and nothing else - the one block that could not say how many figures it was waiting for.

**Built.** `state="loading"` keeps every `LABEL:` and every `SOURCE:` line and bars only the figure, because the labels and the provenance are the schema. A missing reading still prints the vocabulary's word in its own cell.

12. **REGISTER** - from `PARTIAL / TOO MUCH`

**Found.** The line's five parts were printed but never announced: the mark and the separator are `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader ran the label into the figure and read `WHAT CHANGES08`. And the too-much state - a set longer than the page - had no register at all: `RecordPlateSet` printed `SHOWING: 12 OF 240` in its own foot, outside the shape.

**Built.** `Register.astro` prints two runs: the five parts, and a visually hidden line carrying `RegisterSpokenText(...)` - the name, then the figure, with a comma where the eye gets a mark and a slash, because a screen reader says punctuation as characters. The earlier `aria-label` on the `&lt;p&gt;` was dropped by every screen reader, since ARIA prohibits naming the `paragraph` role; and `RegisterWindow(label, showing, total)` is the too-much state as a register, in the grammar every other count uses.

#### What its matrix does not ask

2 conditions, 16 cells unanswered - `MISSING`, `DENIED`. The family's matrix has no column for these, and `/Specimen/States` §THE UNASKED prints the sentence that says why.

#### Its live rows

- **/FACTS** - What the document states as true, and what it states as compared. These are the two blocks a reader checks the project against.
- **/AXES** - Where things sit on one line, and where a claim can be checked along one. The rail has ends and the trace has a source; both are orders.
- **/MEASURES** - How much of something, and what a set of evidence looks like at one size. A figure carries its source; a picture carries its state.
- **/LINES** - The counted line itself - the site's most-printed sentence - in every arm it has, including the two that had no shape before this card.

---

### `# 05` /THE NARRATIVE

**For.** A narrative block is the thing a reader is TOLD: a band opens a subject, a stage explains an order, a figure shows evidence, a well hands over a command, and a failure explains a dead end.

**Read for.** The narrative family's matrix, the three behaviours the brief named by hand, and sixty-two rows of bands, stages, figures, wells, transcripts and failures.

**Its boundary.** The narrative family asks what a block says when the world is unkind to the sentence - no media, one step, ninety steps, a failed turn - and leaves the print medium and the action's absence to the page. A band that is read is not a band that is clicked, and a printed band is the page's fact rather than the block's.

#### What it may never be

The strongest 4 of the 103 sentences this
family's matrix uses to mark a combination impossible. The numbering is the
family's, and the matrix below references it cell by cell.

1. **2 cells.** A figure is one object by definition; a set of one is `RecordPlateSet`, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name.

    `FIGURE / ONE / FIGURE / MANY`

2. **2 cells.** A plate is one object by definition; a set of one is `RecordPlateSet`, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name.

    `PLATE / ONE / PLATE / MANY`

3. **1 cell.** A band opens a subject; it holds no facts of its own, so there is nothing for `partial` to qualify. A fact that is missing is stated by the block inside the band that measured it.

    `BAND / PARTIAL`

4. **1 cell.** A failed action is `RecordFailure`'s three fields. A band that grew a cause and a next step would be a condition block wearing a chapter's grammar.

    `BAND / ERROR`

#### The row that proves it

| MARK | STATE           | PART |
| ---- | --------------- | ---- |
| `12` | EVIDENCE ABSENT | Hero |

**When it is right.** The capture is not in the build: the panel keeps its place and prints the tombstone, never a broken image.

**Why this row.** A block that tells a reader something fails by pointing at evidence that is not there, so the proof is the absent capture: the panel keeps its place and prints the tombstone instead of a broken image.

**See it.** `/Specimen/States` - the family's row on the states gallery; `/Specimen#narrative` - the family's own matrix.
