Every sentence the matrix uses, numbered as the cells reference them:

**1.** 2 cells - A figure is one object by definition; a set of one is `RecordPlateSet`, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name. `FIGURE / ONE / FIGURE / MANY`

**2.** 2 cells - A plate is one object by definition; a set of one is `RecordPlateSet`, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name. `PLATE / ONE / PLATE / MANY`

**3.** 1 cell - A band opens a subject; it holds no facts of its own, so there is nothing for `partial` to qualify. A fact that is missing is stated by the block inside the band that measured it. `BAND / PARTIAL`

**4.** 1 cell - A failed action is `RecordFailure`'s three fields. A band that grew a cause and a next step would be a condition block wearing a chapter's grammar. `BAND / ERROR`

**5.** 1 cell - A band prints no figure and no date, so it has no as-of to be older than. A set that is stale says its age in the block that measured it, which is the block that knows the number. `BAND / STALE`

**6.** 1 cell - A band is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `BAND / DISABLED`

**7.** 1 cell - A band is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `BAND / READ-ONLY`

**8.** 1 cell - A band has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `BAND / REDUCED`

**9.** 1 cell - A band holds a subject, not a set. `ONE` is a count of items, and a band with one item is a band whose body happens to be short. `BAND / ONE`

**10.** 1 cell - A band prints no media. Evidence belongs to a figure or a plate, and a band that framed a picture would be a plate with a heading over it. `BAND / NO MEDIA`

**11.** 1 cell - An entry is a record, not a condition. Its `state` arm carries a reading state (`LOADING`, `ARCHIVED`) and deliberately not a failure: a record that failed is a `RecordFailure` beside the set. `ENTRY / ERROR`

**12.** 1 cell - An entry carries no figure and no date of its own. The age of a record belongs to the archive that filed it or the ledger that measured it, and both print their own `AS OF:`. `ENTRY / STALE`

**13.** 1 cell - A entry is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `ENTRY / DISABLED`

**14.** 1 cell - A entry is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `ENTRY / READ-ONLY`

**15.** 1 cell - A entry has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `ENTRY / REDUCED`

**16.** 1 cell - An entry is one record. `ONE` describes a set, and a set of one is an archive with a single row, which is where the count is printed. `ENTRY / ONE`

**17.** 1 cell - Many entries are an archive or a grid of cards, and the block prints one. A set of many is `RecordArchive`'s shape, not this block's. `ENTRY / MANY`

**18.** 1 cell - An entry holds no media: its anatomy is a marker, a name, chips and a claim. A record with a picture is an entry beside a figure, not an entry holding one. `ENTRY / NO MEDIA`

**19.** 1 cell - A stage prints no as-of. A run's age is a fact about a particular run, and a particular run is a `RecordTranscript` - the stage is the process abstracted out of it. `STAGE / STALE`

**20.** 1 cell - A stage is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `STAGE / DISABLED`

**21.** 1 cell - A stage is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `STAGE / READ-ONLY`

**22.** 1 cell - A stage is a list of steps: an index, a label and one line. A step with a picture is a plate, and a process drawn as pictures is a plate-set. `STAGE / NO MEDIA`

**23.** 1 cell - The stage's two axes are `orientation` and `variant`, and they already answer the two readings of the same data. A third density would be a third composition, which is a second block with one name. `STAGE / DENSE`

**24.** 1 cell - A figure's provenance is a file or a commit, not a date. A figure older than the page is a plate, which prints `AS OF:` on its head, or an instrument, which prints the age beside the figure. `FIGURE / STALE`

**25.** 1 cell - A figure is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `FIGURE / DISABLED`

**26.** 1 cell - A figure is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `FIGURE / READ-ONLY`

**27.** 1 cell - Evidence gets its size. A figure shrunk to fit a dense column is a thumbnail, and a thumbnail is a decoration - which is the one thing a figure is not. `FIGURE / DENSE`

**28.** 1 cell - A plate is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `PLATE / DISABLED`

**29.** 1 cell - A plate is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `PLATE / READ-ONLY`

**30.** 1 cell - A plate is the size it is. A plate shrunk to fit is a thumbnail, and the whole reason this block is not a figure is that the evidence gets the width. `PLATE / DENSE`

**31.** 1 cell - A well prints what it is given, line for line. A command with a line missing is a DIFFERENT command, and the block cannot know which line was meant - so there is no honest partial arm. `WELL / PARTIAL`

**32.** 1 cell - A failed command is a transcript turn or a failure block. The well prints the command and its output; an outcome with a cause and a next step is `RecordTranscript`'s failed turn. `WELL / ERROR`

**33.** 1 cell - A command has no date. Where it came from is its `SOURCE:` line, and a command that is out of date is a command whose source changed - a fact the source line already carries. `WELL / STALE`

**34.** 1 cell - The copy control is ABSENT when there is no clipboard, never disabled: a Jelly control upgraded inside `display: none` has no box, and an inert control is a focus stop that answers nothing. `WELL / DISABLED`

**35.** 1 cell - A well is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `WELL / READ-ONLY`

**36.** 1 cell - A well has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `WELL / REDUCED`

**37.** 1 cell - A well holds text. An image in a recess is a figure, and a figure in a well is a card inside a card's body. `WELL / NO MEDIA`

**38.** 1 cell - A command must not compress: the one thing a well cannot do is reflow its lines. `wrap` is not a density, it is a declaration that the lines are read rather than typed. `WELL / DENSE`

**39.** 1 cell - A transcript is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `TRANSCRIPT / DISABLED`

**40.** 1 cell - A transcript is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `TRANSCRIPT / READ-ONLY`

**41.** 1 cell - A transcript has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `TRANSCRIPT / REDUCED`

**42.** 1 cell - A transcript is verbatim speech and output. A picture of a session is a capture, and a capture is a plate. `TRANSCRIPT / NO MEDIA`

**43.** 1 cell - A transcript is verbatim: a compressed session has dropped the line that mattered. The too-much arm is `window`, which drops nothing silently. `TRANSCRIPT / DENSE`

**44.** 1 cell - A pair prints two claims and one caption. A date belongs to a side's own note - which is where the side's provenance prints - because the caption is about both sides and cannot carry one side's age. `PAIR / STALE`

**45.** 1 cell - A pair is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `PAIR / DISABLED`

**46.** 1 cell - A pair is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `PAIR / READ-ONLY`

**47.** 1 cell - A pair has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `PAIR / REDUCED`

**48.** 1 cell - A pair is two pods by definition. One pod is `RecordAside`, which is the same frame folded - and the routing table sends it there. `PAIR / ONE`

**49.** 1 cell - A third side is a set, and a set is an archive, a matrix or a stage. Three things read against each other is a comparison, not a pair. `PAIR / MANY`

**50.** 1 cell - A pod holds prose or one leaf block, never media. A pair of two pictures is a plate-set, which is the block for many figures of one subject. `PAIR / NO MEDIA`

**51.** 1 cell - Two things are the minimum a comparison can be; there is nothing left to compress. `PAIR / DENSE`

**52.** 1 cell - A hero prints the record's facts, and a fact's age is a property of the row (`LedgerRow.asOf`), which `RecordLedger` prints. The artifact itself has no as-of to be older than. `HERO / STALE`

**53.** 1 cell - A hero is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `HERO / DISABLED`

**54.** 1 cell - A hero is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `HERO / READ-ONLY`

**55.** 1 cell - A hero has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `HERO / REDUCED`

**56.** 1 cell - The hero is the page's one artifact. `ONE` describes a set, and a page has one hero because it has one opening, not because the set is short. `HERO / ONE`

**57.** 1 cell - Two heroes is two openings, and a page has one. A second record opening is a band. `HERO / MANY`

**58.** 1 cell - The artifact gets the screen - that is what makes it the artifact. A dense hero is a band with a card in it. `HERO / DENSE`

**59.** 1 cell - The hero IS the Jelly card: `FieldRecordDataCard` is the surface. A hero inside a card would be two surfaces, which §1.3 forbids. `HERO / IN A CARD`

**60.** 1 cell - An archive's rows are either filed or not. A row whose target is gone prints `state: "gone"` - a tombstone in the record grammar - which is the honest arm, and there is no third. `ARCHIVE / PARTIAL`

**61.** 1 cell - An archive is a set, not an action: it cannot fail. The page that built it can, and that failure is `RecordFailure` in the band above the list. `ARCHIVE / ERROR`

**62.** 1 cell - A archive is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `ARCHIVE / DISABLED`

**63.** 1 cell - A archive is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `ARCHIVE / READ-ONLY`

**64.** 1 cell - An archive is an index: titles, notes and markers. A row with a picture is a card grid, which is a different artifact. `ARCHIVE / NO MEDIA`

**65.** 1 cell - An archive is dense by construction: one row per record, one hairline between. A second density would be the same list with more air, and the air is the band's. `ARCHIVE / DENSE`

**66.** 1 cell - An aside holds one claim - prose, rows or one block. A body with a part unknown is a ledger inside the aside, which is where the partial state prints. `ASIDE / PARTIAL`

**67.** 1 cell - A disclosure cannot fail; it is a `&lt;details&gt;`. A failed action inside it is the block the aside holds, and that block carries the cause and the next step. `ASIDE / ERROR`

**68.** 1 cell - An aside is not dated. A date belongs to the claim it holds - the ledger's row or the note's `AS OF:` - because the aside is the frame, not the fact. `ASIDE / STALE`

**69.** 1 cell - A aside is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `ASIDE / DISABLED`

**70.** 1 cell - A aside is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `ASIDE / READ-ONLY`

**71.** 1 cell - An aside holds prose, rows or one block. A disclosure that holds a picture is a figure with `open`, and that is the block the routing table sends it to. `ASIDE / NO MEDIA`

**72.** 1 cell - An aside is already the compressed form of its subject; folding it further would make it unopenable. `ASIDE / DENSE`

**73.** 1 cell - The summary is the aside's only control, and it is the whole mechanism. An action inside a folded body is an action nobody sees until they have already opened it. `ASIDE / WITH ACTION`

**74.** 1 cell - A note with no claim is a blank in the margin, and a blank is worse than no note. `body` is required and the caller does not mount the block to say nothing. `MARGIN / EMPTY`

**75.** 1 cell - A note states a fact beside a record; it is not an action and cannot fail. A failure in the margin is a `RecordFailure` beside the paragraph it belongs to. `MARGIN / ERROR`

**76.** 1 cell - A note is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `MARGIN / DISABLED`

**77.** 1 cell - A note is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `MARGIN / READ-ONLY`

**78.** 1 cell - A note has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `MARGIN / REDUCED`

**79.** 1 cell - A note is one annotation. `ONE` describes a set, and the margin has no set - a second note is a second margin note. `MARGIN / ONE`

**80.** 1 cell - Many notes are many marginalia, each its own block; the margin is not a list and does not print one. `MARGIN / MANY`

**81.** 1 cell - A note is a claim and a source. A note that had to carry a figure is `RecordInset`, which is the block for exactly that. `MARGIN / NO MEDIA`

**82.** 1 cell - A note is already the densest thing that can carry a source; compressing it would remove the source. `MARGIN / DENSE`

**83.** 1 cell - A inset is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `INSET / DISABLED`

**84.** 1 cell - A inset is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `INSET / READ-ONLY`

**85.** 1 cell - A inset has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `INSET / REDUCED`

**86.** 1 cell - The figure is the reason the block exists; a compressed inset is a margin note with a squashed picture. `INSET / DENSE`

**87.** 1 cell - A stamp with no mark is not a stamp: `mark` and `authority` are required, and an empty one would be a frame that looked like a guarantee and guaranteed nothing. `STAMP / EMPTY`

**88.** 1 cell - A stamp is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `STAMP / DISABLED`

**89.** 1 cell - A stamp is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `STAMP / READ-ONLY`

**90.** 1 cell - A stamp has no motion: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the one fold it prints turns through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `STAMP / REDUCED`

**91.** 1 cell - A stamp's `rows` are the facts that bound the mark, and one fact is a legal stamp. `ONE` here would be a count of a set the stamp does not have - the mark is one. `STAMP / ONE`

**92.** 1 cell - Six facts stack in the stamp's two columns; the count is not the stamp's subject, and the register's figure belongs to a ledger. `STAMP / MANY`

**93.** 1 cell - A stamp is a mark and a register: no picture, no figure. A seal is a glyph and belongs to the artifact, not to the stamp. `STAMP / NO MEDIA`

**94.** 1 cell - A stamp is four lines and a mark; there is nothing to compress, and a compressed stamp is a badge. `STAMP / DENSE`

**95.** 1 cell - A failure is a condition that has already happened. `LOADING` is a state of a reading, and a failure that has not happened is not one - the block has no arm for a failure in progress. `FAILURE / LOADING`

**96.** 1 cell - The three fields are required. A failure with no symptom is a blank in a condition block, and a blank condition is a lie about what the reader is looking at. `FAILURE / EMPTY`

**97.** 1 cell - A failure is documented at a commit, not dated: its `SOURCE:` line says where it is written, and that is the only provenance a condition can have. `FAILURE / STALE`

**98.** 1 cell - A failure is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `FAILURE / DISABLED`

**99.** 1 cell - A failure is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `FAILURE / READ-ONLY`

**100.** 1 cell - A failure is one condition. `ONE` describes a set, and a set of failures is a table of them - each its own block, side by side. `FAILURE / ONE`

**101.** 1 cell - Three failures side by side align on SYMPTOM, CAUSE and NEXT because each is its own block. The block prints one; the alignment is the composition's. `FAILURE / MANY`

**102.** 1 cell - A failure is four fields. A screenshot of a failure is a figure beside it, not inside it - the block's own note says a stack trace is a well beside it. `FAILURE / NO MEDIA`

**103.** 1 cell - The three fields ARE the density. A failure with a shorter cause is a failure that stopped explaining itself. `FAILURE / DENSE`

#### What the exploration changed

1. **BAND** - from `EMPTY / LOADING`

    **Found.** A chapter whose subject was not written yet rendered nothing: the band printed its heading and stopped, so a reader saw a title with a hole under it and no way to tell a missing set from a short one.

    **Built.** `Band.state` with `Band.empty`: the head, the standfirst, the index strip and the footnote all print, and the body becomes the composed absence - `◎`, `STATUS:`, the caller's sentence. The band's own footnote is still the last thing read, so the next step sits under the absence.

2. **BAND** - from `DENSE`

    **Found.** Every band spent the chapter interval and the chapter heading tier, so a band used as a section inside a hero or a card opened at the volume of a page movement.

    **Built.** `Band.dense` prints the head at the heading tier and the body at the tight step, with the chapter interval dropped: a section of an artifact reads as a section, and the page's air stays the page's.

3. **ENTRY** - from `EMPTY / LOADING / ARCHIVED`

    **Found.** An entry's `body` was required, so a record that was being read, or one that had been retired, could not be printed at all - the set either omitted the slot or lied with a placeholder sentence.

    **Built.** `Entry.state` keeps the index, the name and the chips and replaces only the claim: `empty` and `loading` print the composed absence, `archived` prints the claim with `STATUS: ARCHIVED` above it in the quiet tone. The record is still filed, and the list still knows where it sits.

4. **ENTRY** - from `FACTS`

    **Found.** An entry that carried three facts had to spell them into its paragraph, so a set of records that were comparable as facts could not be read as a register.

    **Built.** `Entry.facts` prints the record's own `&lt;dl&gt;` under the claim - the entry's grammar, not a mounted `RecordLedger`, because a leaf may not hold a block (§4.2). `Entry.note` gives the record one `SOURCE:` line, which is the only place it had to say where it is filed.

5. **ENTRY** - from `DENSE`

    **Found.** `surface="bare"` removed the frame but kept the entry's tall anatomy, so ten records inside one card still read as ten cards' worth of air.

    **Built.** `Entry.dense` is the register reading: marker and name on one line, chips beside them, the claim under at the body tier - a hairline between rows instead of a frame around each. Never a smaller type.

6. **STAGE** - from `PARTIAL / ERROR`

    **Found.** A rail of steps said nothing about where the run was. A build that had stopped at stage three printed the same nine items as a build that had never started, so the block described a process and not a run.

    **Built.** `RecordStage.current` names the step the run is at by the index the caller wrote; that step prints `aria-current="step"`, the attested square and the divider's rule. A step's own `state` prints the vocabulary's word - `INTERRUPTED` on the step that stopped - so the rail carries a run's position without becoming a stepper.

7. **STAGE** - from `LONG`

    **Found.** A stage's line is one line, and every step that needed a paragraph either broke that rule or lost the paragraph. The block had no level between the line and the page.

    **Built.** `Stage.detail` turns the step's line into a `&lt;details&gt;` summary with the paragraph one level in: closed, the rail keeps its reading rhythm; open, the step explains itself. No script - the browser owns the disclosure, and its own in-page search finds the text while it is closed.

8. **STAGE** - from `EMPTY / ONE / MANY`

    **Found.** A stage with no steps printed an empty `&lt;ol&gt;`; a stage with one step printed a rail that looked like a failure; a stage with nine wrapped into a shape nobody had composed.

    **Built.** `stages.length === 0` is now the composed absence in the frame's own grammar, and one step and nine steps are both printed by the same two arms - the rail wraps, the plates tile two across, and the caller's numbering is never re-derived from a position.

9. **FIGURE** - from `NO MEDIA / LONG`

    **Found.** A figure with a caption longer than its image had no answer: the caption ran to the measure cap and the provenance sat under it, so the one case the brief names by hand read as a paragraph that happened to follow a picture.

    **Built.** `Figure.open` folds the caption's apparatus: the summary is the caption itself, so shutting it loses nothing, and the open arm prints the `SOURCE:` row, the `〈FIGURE〉` folio and `→ OPEN THE SOURCE` - the full-size evidence, without a lightbox. With no `src` and no children the block still prints the caption alone and draws no frame around nothing.

10. **FIGURE** - from `PARTIAL / ERROR`

**Found.** The tombstone printed its state word and stopped, so a reader told that the capture was interrupted had no next step - a dead end wearing an adverse state's grammar.

**Built.** `Figure.next` prints `NEXT:` inside the tombstone, the way a plate already did, and the channel placement's missing provenance prints `SOURCE: UNAVAILABLE` instead of omitting the row.

11. **PLATE** - from `PARTIAL / NO MEDIA`

**Found.** A plate with a state and no `next` printed the state and stopped: the same dead end as a figure, in the block whose whole subject is the capture that is not in the build.

**Built.** `plate.next` now falls back to `NEXT: UNAVAILABLE` in the quiet tone, so the row always prints and always says whether a next step exists. `Plate.open` folds the channel's apparatus - the reading, the manifest's facts, the source and `→ OPEN THE CAPTURE` - under the `FIGURE:` claim.

12. **WELL** - from `LONG / MANY`

**Found.** The body was `white-space: pre` and scrolled sideways, which is right for a command and wrong for the config and output a well also carries: a 300-character value forced a reader to scroll a recess to find the end of a line. A two-hundred-line log printed all two hundred.

**Built.** `Well.wrap` is the caller's declaration that the lines are read rather than typed: `pre-wrap` with a hanging indent, every character printed. `Well.window` prints the first N lines and `SHOWING: N OF M` on the foot while the copy payload stays whole - the reader who copies gets the file.

13. **WELL** - from `EMPTY / PARTIAL`

**Found.** A well with no lines printed an empty recess under a title bar, and there was no way to say `this command is not documented yet` - the recess was indistinguishable from a well whose content failed to load.

**Built.** `Well.state` with `Well.empty`: the bar keeps its label so the reader knows WHICH command is missing, and the recess prints `STATUS:` and the sentence. `Well.note` gives the well one line for what the command assumes, printed in its own foot rather than as a paragraph beside it.

14. **TRANSCRIPT** - from `ERROR`

**Found.** A failed turn printed `INTERRUPTED` in the stamp column and nothing else: a red word where the cause and the next step belong, and no way to say what the session could do about it.

**Built.** `Turn.cause` and `Turn.next` print under the failed turn's line in a row that spans the grid, and `Transcript.retry` prints the session's one way back on the foot - once, not repeated under every turn that stopped at the same place.

15. **PAIR** - from `EMPTY / PARTIAL`

**Found.** A pod with no body rendered a title bar over nothing, so a comparison with one side missing read as a card with a gap - and the reader could not tell which side was missing.

**Built.** `PairPod.empty` prints the composed absence inside the pod and keeps its bar; `PairPod.state` prints the side's own word in that bar; `PairPod.note` gives the side its own provenance, which the shared caption cannot carry.

16. **PAIR** - from `REST`

**Found.** The pair's caption made its statement at the foot, after both sides had been read - so the one thing that made two columns one artifact arrived last.

**Built.** `Pair.relation` prints the relation in the gutter the pair already draws: vertical on wide screens, a row between the stacked pods on narrow ones. The caption still closes the artifact; the relation now says how the two sides bear on each other where the eye is.

17. **HERO** - from `NO MEDIA / ERROR`

**Found.** A hero whose capture was not in the build either lost its evidence panel - collapsing the artifact into one column - or framed a broken image, because `HeroEvidence` required `src` and `alt` and had no absent arm.

**Built.** `HeroEvidence.state` and `.next` print the tombstone in the evidence panel: the pair keeps its `49fr / 1px / 51fr`, the hairline gutter stays, and the panel says what is missing and what to do about it.

18. **ARCHIVE** - from `EMPTY / ONE / MANY`

**Found.** An archive with no entries printed its header, its `0`, and nothing under them - the one state the brief calls `empty` was a hole. A two-hundred-entry index printed all two hundred, and a row whose target had gone printed a dead link.

**Built.** `Archive.state` with `Archive.empty` prints the counted zero and the composed absence; `Archive.window` prints the first N rows and `SHOWING: N OF M` on the foot; `ArchiveEntry.state = "gone"` prints a tombstone row with the route it used to have. One entry is printed by the same arms and the count says `1`.

19. **ASIDE** - from `ONE / MANY / LOADING`

**Found.** A folded section gave the reader no way to decide whether to open it: the summary was a label, and the body's extent was invisible until it had already been read.

**Built.** `Aside.count` prints `〈04〉` on the summary, derived from the rows or paragraphs the aside holds unless the caller knows the real extent. `Aside.state = "loading"` prints the state word on the bar and three hairlines in the body - the shape of the disclosure before its content.

20. **MARGIN** - from `STALE`

**Found.** A note could say `LOADING` or `UNAVAILABLE` but not WHEN its claim was true, so the one annotation whose job is provenance was the one that could not be dated.

**Built.** `MarginNote.asOf` prints `AS OF:` beside the state on one register row above the claim: the two facts that decide how much the note is worth arrive before the note itself.

21. **INSET** - from `MANY / PARTIAL`

**Found.** A measure figure of three bars printed three claims and never their sum, so the one figure the inset exists to draw could not be read as a whole. An absent figure had no next step.

**Built.** `InsetFigure.total` prints the caller's sum under the bars on the divider's rule - the caller's arithmetic, never the block's - and `InsetFigure.next` prints `NEXT:` inside the absent frame, falling back to `UNAVAILABLE`.

22. **STAMP** - from `STALE / WITH ACTION`

**Found.** A stamp said what made it true and never when it stopped being true, and it had no way to point at the route that checks it: the authority was a sentence the reader had to take on trust.

**Built.** `Stamp.expires` prints `EXPIRES:` with the facts that bound the mark, and `Stamp.verify` prints `→ LABEL` under the authority - the one destination a stamp needs, printed as a link and never as a button, and suppressed on a withdrawn mark because a withdrawn mark has nothing left to verify.

23. **FAILURE** - from `PARTIAL / ERROR`

**Found.** The brief's own case - a failure with no recovery path - printed an empty `NEXT:` value or a sentence pointing nowhere. The block had no way to say that the dead end was the finding.

**Built.** `next` that is empty or `UNAVAILABLE` prints the vocabulary's word in the value's place and marks the block `--dead-end`, so the absence of a next step is visibly a fact. `Failure.recovery` prints the destination the sentence names as the block's one link, and `Failure.detail` folds the reproduction under the three fields.

#### What its matrix does not ask

4 conditions, 60 cells unanswered - `MISSING`, `DENIED`, `NO ACTION`, `ON PAPER`. The family's matrix has no column for these, and `/Specimen/States` §THE UNASKED prints the sentence that says why.

#### Its live rows

- **/THE FRAMES** - The blocks that hold a subject: the band, the entry, the opening, the comparison and the disclosure. A frame is read before it is looked at.
- **/THE SEQUENCES** - The blocks that hold an order: a process, an index and a session. Each one is read in the direction its data runs, and each one has a too-many arm.
- **/THE EVIDENCE** - The blocks that show something: a figure in a column, a plate at plate scale and an inset in a margin. All three answer what a picture proves, at three distances.
- **/THE APPARATUS** - The blocks that let the document prove itself: the command, the mark, the note and the failure. None of them is prose, and none of them is decoration.

---

### `# 06` /THE FRAME

**For.** The frame decides whether content can be read at all - and its one law is that nothing here is a card: a shell holds tracks, a track holds bands, a band holds records, and a card is a record's surface.

**Read for.** The shell, the rail, the seam, the plate and the surface states, plus the five compositions a page shell has to survive - no rail, two rails, a shell inside a shell, a pane pair at 640px, and a plate with no image.

**Its boundary.** The frame family asks its own compositions - no rail, two rails, a shell inside a shell, a pane pair at 640px, a plate with no image - and leaves the states of a record to the record. A shell holds tracks: it states no fact, points at no target, and carries no action of its own.

#### What it may never be

The strongest 4 of the 118 sentences this
family's matrix uses to mark a combination impossible. The numbering is the
family's, and the matrix below references it cell by cell.

1. **4 cells.** A badge is a word or a row on a line, not a page composition: the rail count of the page it sits on is the shell's fact, and a badge that re-composed because the page had two rails would be a badge with an opinion about layout.

    `BADGE / NO RAIL / BADGE / TWO RAILS / BADGE / IN A CARD / BADGE / AT 640`

2. **4 cells.** A state badge is a word or a row on a line, not a page composition: the rail count of the page it sits on is the shell's fact, and a badge that re-composed because the page had two rails would be a badge with an opinion about layout.

    `STATEBADGE / NO RAIL / STATEBADGE / TWO RAILS / STATEBADGE / IN A CARD / STATEBADGE / AT 640`

3. **3 cells.** A chip run is a word or a row on a line, not a page composition: the rail count of the page it sits on is the shell's fact, and a badge that re-composed because the page had two rails would be a badge with an opinion about layout.

    `CHIPS / NO RAIL / CHIPS / TWO RAILS / CHIPS / IN A CARD`

4. **2 cells.** A surface shell is one object by definition; a set of one is one page's frame, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name.

    `SHELL / ONE / SHELL / MANY`

#### The row that proves it

| MARK       | STATE  | PART      |

| `FRAME_04` | AT 640 | PAGESHELL |

**When it is right.** The same two-rail reading page at a phone's width: both rails become ruled registers above the paper, in reading order, and nothing is folded away.

**Why this row.** The frame decides whether content can be read at all, and the phone is where it is usually given up on: at 640 both rails become ruled registers above the paper, in reading order, and nothing is folded away.

**See it.** `/Specimen/States` - the family's row on the states gallery; `/Specimen#frame` - the family's own matrix.

**9.** 2 cells - A lifecycle register is a word or a row on a line, not a page composition: the rail count of the page it sits on is the shell's fact, and a badge that re-composed because the page had two rails would be a badge with an opinion about layout. `LIFE / NO RAIL / LIFE / TWO RAILS`

**10.** 2 cells - A page shell is one object by definition; a set of one is one page's composition, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name. `PAGESHELL / ONE / PAGESHELL / MANY`

**11.** 2 cells - A headnote is one object by definition; a set of one is one sheet's opening, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name. `EDGE LEAF / ONE / EDGE LEAF / MANY`

**14.** 2 cells - A print row is one object by definition; a set of one is one command, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name. `PRINT / ONE / PRINT / MANY`

**15.** 1 cell - A surface shell is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `SHELL / DISABLED`

**16.** 1 cell - A shell is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `SHELL / READ-ONLY`

**17.** 1 cell - A shell has no motion of its own: its state changes are ink, rule and space, and the two folds it prints turn through the mark layer, which is already gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`. `SHELL / REDUCED`

#### What the exploration changed

1. **LIFE** - from `PARTIAL / the whole family's vocabulary`

    **Found.** Four pages answered the same question in four adjectives - "Coming Soon" on the portal, "Feature Gated" on the download masthead, "Disabled" in the dashboard, "Beta" in an article - and none of them could be counted, compared or audited. The state vocabulary said what a surface was DOING and had no word for how far along it was.

    **Built.** `Surface/State.ts` carries `Life`: five words (`LIVE`, `BETA`, `PLANNED`, `RETIRED`, `UNAVAILABLE`), each with its tone and the sentence that decides between them, and `SurfaceLife.astro` is its one renderer - the register head, the word in force, all five steps with the one in force marked, and the gloss. `SurfaceHead` and `SurfaceShell` take `life` + `lifeNote`, so a surface declares its maturity in the same place it declares its status. A word outside the five prints `UNAVAILABLE` and the block says so, because an adjective is not a word from the table.

2. **PLATE** - from `NO IMAGE`

    **Found.** A plate with no `media`, no `trace` and no slot printed its frame as an empty white field at the plate's full height - a figure that was a hole, which reads as a page that failed rather than a plate with a fact to state. The brief named this composition by hand.

    **Built.** `ShellPlate.absence` - `{ status, wouldBe, whyNot, next }` - prints the composed absence INSIDE the plate's own frame, at the plate's own height, in the record's `KEY:` grammar. The frame stays a plate: a figure does not become a card because its evidence is missing, and the three rows are the same three every absence on the site prints.

3. **RAIL** - from `MANY / ONE`

    **Found.** Every page with a rail of sections built a second rail beside `ShellRail` - the manual's tree, the legal clause list, the contact record column - because the primitive could hold one flat list and no groups. Five rails became seven.

    **Built.** `ShellRail.groups` - a rail of sections, each with its own sub-register line and its own count counted from its own rows, in one `&lt;ol&gt;` per group. The rows keep the reserved mark column across every group, which is the only reason to group a register instead of stacking two rails. `items` stays the flat form and is still what most callers pass.

4. **RAIL** - from `EMPTY / LOADING`

    **Found.** A rail whose destinations had not been read printed its register line and then an empty `&lt;ol&gt;` - a count over nothing, which is the exact defect the register line exists to prevent.

    **Built.** `ShellRail.state` (`rest` | `empty` | `loading`) with `empty` and `keys`: `empty` prints `◎ UNAVAILABLE` and the caller's sentence inside the rail; `loading` prints the keys with their values barred, `aria-hidden`, static. The register line stays either way, because the head is what names the thing that is not there.

5. **RAIL** - from `DENSE / IN A CARD`

    **Found.** A rail in a drawer, a pane or a card spent the same air as a rail at the page's edge, so ten rows of a rail inside a card were taller than the card's own content.

    **Built.** `ShellRail.dense` - the same rows at the tight step. The mark column, the notes and the meta all stay: a dense rail is a rail in less air, never a rail with less in it.

6. **PANES** - from `EMPTY / LOADING`

    **Found.** A pane whose instrument had not arrived printed its head and then an empty body - a pane that read as failed rather than as a pane with a fact to state. The pair had no way to say "one half is not here yet" without dropping the half.

    **Built.** Each pane takes `state`, `empty` and `keys`; a pane with no slot is `empty` by construction. The absent arm prints `STATUS:` and the pane's own sentence (or the keys and barred values), under the same head, with the seam still drawn - so a pair with one absent half is still one instrument divided.

7. **REGION** - from `EMPTY / LOADING`

    **Found.** A region whose record had not arrived rendered its index, its `h2` and its standfirst and then nothing: a heading with a hole under it, which reads as a page that failed to load rather than a region with a fact to state.

    **Built.** `SurfaceRegion.state` (`rest` | `empty` | `loading`) with `empty` and `keys`: the two arms every other block in the family has, printed under the same head, in the record grammar - `◎ UNAVAILABLE` and a sentence, or the keys with their values barred. `dense` is the region inside a card or a pane.

8. **PAGESHELL** - from `NO RAIL / TWO RAILS`

    **Found.** The declaration strip printed what the LANGUAGE gives (`GIVES: RAIL␁MEASURE␁MARGIN`) over pages that had taken one, two or none of those tracks, so the strip could describe a page that did not exist - and the two-rail and no-rail compositions were invisible on the page itself.

    **Built.** `PageShell` now prints a second fact, `TRACKS:`, counted from the slots that are actually present (`RAIL␁PAPER␁MARGIN`, `PAPER␁MARGIN`, `RAIL␁PAPER`). The language's offer and the page's take are two different facts and the strip states both. Printed only when a side track is present, because `PAPER` alone is not news.

9. **FRAME RAIL** - from `MANY / the register's own rule`

    **Found.** The dossier's thumb index printed `# INDEX:` over ten tabs and no figure - a register line without its count, which is the one defect `RegisterLine.ts` exists to remove, in the frame itself.

    **Built.** `FrameRailCount` prints `FrameExtent` (`FrameSections.length`) after the label, separated by U+2001. In the 2.25rem column the tabs ARE the figure, so the count is hidden there and printed in the drawer, where the list needs its extent stated.

10. **REGISTER** - from `MANY`

**Found.** A legend of eight states printed as eight stacked rows: a set read as a list, at the height of a page section, when the reader's job was to compare the words.

**Built.** `SurfaceState.columns={2}` reads the register across at 640px and above, and `dense` is its tight step. The rows keep their order - the columns fill left to right - so the array's reading order is the register's.

11. **ABSENT** - from `ERROR`

**Found.** The absence's `NEXT:` row was its only action, so a failed request could state the way forward and not the retry - and `ShellState`'s error arm has had both since it was written.

**Built.** `SurfaceAbsent.retry` prints a `RETRY:` row under `NEXT:`, so a reader whose action failed is owed the command and the alternative in the same composition. `dense` is the absence inside a card or a pane.

#### What its matrix does not ask

4 conditions, 80 cells unanswered - `MISSING`, `DENIED`, `IN A BAND`, `NO ACTION`. The family's matrix has no column for these, and `/Specimen/States` §THE UNASKED prints the sentence that says why.

#### Its live rows

- **/THE FRAMES** - The five languages and the three compositions the brief named: no rail, two rails, a shell inside a shell, the same page at 640px, and the one-artifact page that declares nothing.
- **/THE PANES** - Two instruments with one seam: the three ratios, the stack that is a choice rather than a fallback, the pair at 640px, and the arms a pair needs when one half has not arrived.
- **/THE RAILS** - One register of destinations in every state it has: rest, in force, statements, one row, twenty-six, groups, empty, loading, dense, long and the closing foot.
- **/THE PLATES** - The plate's five arms and its two bleeds - including the one the brief named by hand: a plate with no image, which is now a composition rather than an empty frame.
- **/THE SURFACES** - The app surface's own parts: the lifecycle vocabulary at work, a region's two adverse arms, the register read across, the shared readout, the badge and chip runs and the absence's retry.
- **/THE STATE ARMS** - The three readings of the nine adverse states the sheet's own band does not print: the dense step, the bare arm inside a card, and a partial reading that keeps the facts it has.
- **/THE EDGES** - The frame's first band and its last: the leaf's unfiled and stale arms, the turn's two dead ends, and the colophon's print row.

---

### `# 07` /THE READING

**For.** Furniture fails by losing the reader: a rail that does not say where you are, a contents list that does not say where you are in the page, a folio that does not say how far you have got.

**Read for.** The rail, the contents, the index card, the article, the appendix, the folio, the see-also and the leader - a document with one section, with ninety, a heading wider than the rail, and a strip at 640px.

**Its boundary.** The reading family asks where the reader is - one section, ninety sections, a heading wider than the rail, no summary, no cross-reference, a strip at 640px - and leaves the motion arm to the blocks that move. Furniture that is already in place does not animate into place, and a rail of destinations is not a set a band holds.

#### The row that proves it

| MARK      | STATE  | PART      |
| --------- | ------ | --------- |
| `READ_06` | NINETY | DOCLAYOUT |

**When it is right.** A document with ninety sections: the contents register folds itself and goes dense, so the tree keeps the rail's scroll instead of a slit.

**Why this row.** Furniture fails by losing the reader, and ninety sections is the case that does it: the contents register folds itself and goes dense so the tree keeps the rail's scroll instead of a slit.

**See it.** `/Specimen/States` - the family's row on the states gallery; `/Specimen#reading` - the family's own matrix.

**7.** 1 cell - A documentation shell is read at build time: the rail, the paper and the margin are server-rendered and the one island inside it (the mobile tree) hydrates over rows the server already printed so there is no state in which the block exists and its content has not arrived. `DOCLAYOUT / LOADING`

**8.** 1 cell - A shell carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to the page's apparatus - a folio, a ledger row, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `DOCLAYOUT / STALE`

**9.** 1 cell - A documentation shell is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `DOCLAYOUT / DISABLED`

**10.** 1 cell - A documentation shell is a page's container, not a record's surface: inside a card it would print a page's rail inside a record. The composition the frame family prints as `IN A CARD` is `PageShell`'s, and this shell is not one. `DOCLAYOUT / IN A CARD`

**11.** 1 cell - This block IS the rail: a rail's own rail count is not a composition it has. The page that has no rail is the Rust surface, and it wears `DocArticle` without this shell. `DOCLAYOUT / NO RAIL`

**12.** 1 cell - A article shell is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `DOCARTICLE / DISABLED`

**13.** 1 cell - A reading shell has no tight step: the measure and the prose rhythm are the article's, and a denser article is a shorter article - which is an edit, not a state. `DOCARTICLE / DENSE`

**14.** 1 cell - An article shell is a page's column: inside a card it would print a page inside a record. The paper it prints is already the white insert the card would be. `DOCARTICLE / IN A CARD`

**15.** 1 cell - The shell prints no action: the pager at the foot is the page's, and the shell's slot is prose. A control inside the header would be a control inside a nameplate. `DOCARTICLE / WITH ACTION`

**16.** 1 cell - A contents register is read at build time: the rows are the headings `render()` reported, so the list and the document are written in the same pass so there is no state in which the block exists and its content has not arrived. `DOCCONTENTS / LOADING`

**17.** 1 cell - A contents list cannot fail on its own: its rows are the document's headings, and a page whose headings failed has no list to print - the paper's absence is `DocArticle`'s arm. `DOCCONTENTS / ERROR`

**18.** 1 cell - A contents register carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to the page's folio or its strip, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `DOCCONTENTS / STALE`

**21.** 1 cell - A contents list is read at build time: the rows are the document's headings and the ids are the pipeline's, written in the same pass so there is no state in which the block exists and its content has not arrived. `DOCCONTENTSLIST / LOADING`

**23.** 1 cell - A list of anchors has no failure arm: a target that moved is a broken anchor the page prints, not a state the list can invent. `DOCCONTENTSLIST / ERROR`

**24.** 1 cell - A contents list carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to the page's folio or its strip, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `DOCCONTENTSLIST / STALE`

**28.** 1 cell - A layer map is read at build time: the entries are the section's pages in collection order, passed by the page so there is no state in which the block exists and its content has not arrived. `DOCLAYER / LOADING`

**29.** 1 cell - A map has no failure arm: the pages either exist in the collection or they do not, and a disclosure that could not read them is the empty arm. `DOCLAYER / ERROR`

**30.** 1 cell - A layer map carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to the page's folio, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `DOCLAYER / STALE`

**32.** 1 cell - A map is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `DOCLAYER / READ-ONLY`

**33.** 1 cell - A disclosure row has no tight step: closed it is one line at chapter distance, and a denser row would be a row in the prose above it. `DOCLAYER / DENSE`

**34.** 1 cell - A layer map closes an article: inside a card it would be a map inside a record, and the article above it is the surface. `DOCLAYER / IN A CARD`

**35.** 1 cell - An index section with no rows is dropped by `BuildDocIndex` before it reaches this block: an empty chapter is not a chapter, and a band with a count of zero would be a chapter that apologises for itself. `DOCINDEX / EMPTY`

**36.** 1 cell - A chapter is read at build time: the rows are the collection's pages, read at build time and ordered by `SectionOrder` so there is no state in which the block exists and its content has not arrived. `DOCINDEX / LOADING`

**37.** 1 cell - A chapter has no failure arm: the pages it files are the collection's, and a collection that could not be read is a build that does not run. `DOCINDEX / ERROR`

**38.** 1 cell - A chapter carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to each card's page - its strip, its folio, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `DOCINDEX / STALE`

**39.** 1 cell - A chapter is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `DOCINDEX / DISABLED`

**40.** 1 cell - A chapter is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `DOCINDEX / READ-ONLY`

**41.** 1 cell - The chapter is a band and a grid: its density is the grid's capacity line (`--row-floor`), not a tight step, and a denser grid is a narrower card. `DOCINDEX / DENSE`

**42.** 1 cell - A chapter is a band wrapping a grid: inside a card it would be a page's chapter inside a record, and a card inside a card is the one composition the identity forbids. `DOCINDEX / IN A CARD`

**43.** 1 cell - A card is read at build time: the card renders one page's record, and the record is the collection's so there is no state in which the block exists and its content has not arrived. `DOCCARD / LOADING`

**44.** 1 cell - A card has no failure arm: it renders one page's label, note and href, and a page whose record failed is a page that is not in the collection. `DOCCARD / ERROR`

**45.** 1 cell - A card carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to the page it leads to - its strip, its folio, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `DOCCARD / STALE`

**46.** 1 cell - A card is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `DOCCARD / DISABLED`

**47.** 1 cell - A card is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `DOCCARD / READ-ONLY`

**48.** 1 cell - A card's density is the grid's: the capacity line decides how many fit, and a card with less air inside is a card whose note is closer to its title for no reason. `DOCCARD / DENSE`

**49.** 1 cell - A card is one object by definition; a set is a chapter's grid, which is `DocIndex`'s, and a block that answered both would be two blocks with one name. `DOCCARD / ONE`

**50.** 1 cell - A card IS a record's surface: a card inside a card is the one composition the identity forbids, and the card's `jelly-card` is already the surface it sits on. `DOCCARD / IN A CARD`

**51.** 1 cell - A failed read is the empty arm: the panel states what would be here, and there is no retry a printed page can offer - the retry is a rebuild. `DOCAPPENDIX / ERROR`

**52.** 1 cell - A appendix panel carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to the page's folio or the record it reads, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `DOCAPPENDIX / STALE`

**53.** 1 cell - A appendix panel is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `DOCAPPENDIX / DISABLED`

**54.** 1 cell - A panel is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `DOCAPPENDIX / READ-ONLY`

**55.** 1 cell - The panel is one artifact at the band's rhythm; a denser panel is a table, and the site has one of those where it means a comparison. `DOCAPPENDIX / DENSE`

**56.** 1 cell - The panel IS the surface: a card inside the panel would be a card inside a card, and the appendix's `h2` above it already opens the subject. `DOCAPPENDIX / IN A CARD`

**57.** 1 cell - A summary is `DocArticle`'s - the appendix's own sentence is its `Lede`, which is required: this block never prints one, so its absence changes nothing here - which is the cell's answer, not an evasion. `DOCAPPENDIX / NO SUMMARY`

**58.** 1 cell - A rustdoc site that fails to load fails INSIDE the frame: the viewer cannot read it (sandboxed, cross-origin), and the browser's own error page is the only honest report. Inventing an error arm would be inventing a fact. `RUSTVIEWER / ERROR`

**59.** 1 cell - The rustdoc output tracks the Current branch; its age is the crate's, and the page states the branch in its own copy above the viewer - a second as-of in the tab bar would be a second source. `RUSTVIEWER / STALE`

**60.** 1 cell - The viewer's tabs are never disabled: a crate that cannot be shown is not a tab, and a disabled tab is a control saying "not for you" about a document the reader came to read. `RUSTVIEWER / DISABLED`

**61.** 1 cell - The viewer is read-only in the sense that matters - it shows a rustdoc site and edits nothing - so `read-only` names no arm it could have. The frame's sandbox is the same fact stated in markup. `RUSTVIEWER / READ-ONLY`

**62.** 1 cell - A tab bar and a frame have no tight step: the bar is one row of labels and the frame is as tall as the viewport it is read in. `RUSTVIEWER / DENSE`

**63.** 1 cell - The viewer is a surface with a frame in it: inside a card it would be a frame inside a frame, and the frame's own border would be the second. `RUSTVIEWER / IN A CARD`

**64.** 1 cell - A crate group with one crate is the `ONE` cell; a section is not a thing the viewer holds - the register of crates is `DocIndex`'s. `RUSTVIEWER / ONE SECTION`

**65.** 1 cell - The viewer prints crate names, not headings: a heading is the page's, above it. `RUSTVIEWER / LONG HEADING`

**66.** 1 cell - A summary is `DocArticle`'s, above the viewer: this block never prints one, so its absence changes nothing here - which is the cell's answer, not an evasion. `RUSTVIEWER / NO SUMMARY`

**67.** 1 cell - An `&lt;iframe&gt;` does not print: the viewer's frame is a live surface, and a printed page would show the tab bar over a blank rectangle. The crates are listed as links above it, which is what prints. `RUSTVIEWER / ON PAPER`

**68.** 1 cell - A reading surface is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `READINGDOCUMENT / DISABLED`

**69.** 1 cell - A surface is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `READINGDOCUMENT / READ-ONLY`

**70.** 1 cell - A document read at prose rhythm has no tight step: the measure is the surface's and the clauses are the document's. A denser document is an edit. `READINGDOCUMENT / DENSE`

**71.** 1 cell - The reading surface is the page's paper: inside a card it would be a document inside a record. The legal pages' white card is the body's own class, not a wrapper around the surface. `READINGDOCUMENT / IN A CARD`

**72.** 1 cell - A foot is two printed registers; there is no action for an error to belong to, and the failure's composition is `ShellState`'s. `BANDFOOT / ERROR`

**73.** 1 cell - A band foot is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `BANDFOOT / DISABLED`

**74.** 1 cell - A foot is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `BANDFOOT / READ-ONLY`

**75.** 1 cell - The foot is the smallest composition on the site - one rule, two registers. A denser one is a folio, which is a different block. `BANDFOOT / DENSE`

**76.** 1 cell - A foot closes one band: a document's section count is the page's figure, printed by a folio or a register, not by a foot's rows. `BANDFOOT / ONE SECTION`

**77.** 1 cell - A band's foot prints a handful of references and a folio; ninety is a document's count and it is a figure, not rows. The block that lists ninety is `Leader` or `DocContents`. `BANDFOOT / NINETY`

**78.** 1 cell - A foot prints a part, a count, an as-of and references - not a heading. The band's heading is the band's. `BANDFOOT / LONG HEADING`

**79.** 1 cell - A summary is `DocArticle`'s, and the band's own standfirst: this block never prints one, so its absence changes nothing here - which is the cell's answer, not an evasion. `BANDFOOT / NO SUMMARY`

**80.** 1 cell - A folio's place is required - an ordinal and a part. A folio with neither is not a folio; it is a line of nothing at the foot of a band, which is the defect the block exists to remove. `FOLIO / EMPTY`

**81.** 1 cell - A folio prints what the page read. It has no state of its own, and a barred ordinal would be a place the reader cannot be told. `FOLIO / LOADING`

**82.** 1 cell - A folio is a printed line: there is no action for an error to belong to. `FOLIO / ERROR`

**83.** 1 cell - A folio is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `FOLIO / DISABLED`

**84.** 1 cell - A folio is read-only by construction - it is markup and CSS with nothing to edit - so `read-only` names no arm this block could have. `FOLIO / READ-ONLY`

**85.** 1 cell - The folio is one line at the meta tier; there is nothing under it to tighten. `FOLIO / DENSE`

**86.** 1 cell - A folio prints a document's part and its figures; a section is a row in `DocContents`. `FOLIO / ONE SECTION`

**87.** 1 cell - A folio counts; it does not list. Ninety is a figure it prints (`90 SECTIONS`), not ninety rows - the block that lists ninety is `DocContents` or `Leader`. `FOLIO / NINETY`

**88.** 1 cell - A folio prints a part, not a heading. `FOLIO / LONG HEADING`

**89.** 1 cell - A folio is printed, not clicked: the ordinal and the part are text. A folio that linked would be a pager. `FOLIO / WITH ACTION`

**90.** 1 cell - A reference list has no failure arm: a route that is gone is a tombstone the page prints, and a register that invented an error state would be inventing a fact about a link. `SEE / ERROR`

**91.** 1 cell - A cross-reference register carries no as-of of its own: an age belongs to the page's folio, and a block that invented one would be the one figure on the page with no source. `SEE / STALE`

**92.** 1 cell - A cross-reference register is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `SEE / DISABLED`

**93.** 1 cell - Two rows at the foot of a band; a tight step would be a list with no air in the smallest composition on the site. `SEE / DENSE`

**94.** 1 cell - A see-also is not a document's section: the sections are `DocContents`'. `SEE / ONE SECTION`

**95.** 1 cell - A see-also is a handful of references. Ninety is an index, and the site has `Leader` and `DocContents` for that. `SEE / NINETY`

**96.** 1 cell - A register prints routes, not headings. `SEE / LONG HEADING`

**97.** 1 cell - A register has no failure arm: a set that could not be read is the empty state with its sentence, which is the same composition with a truer cause. `LEADER / ERROR`

**98.** 1 cell - A leader prints figures, not dates: an entry's date is its `meta`, and the register's age is the page's - the block derives none of it. `LEADER / STALE`

**99.** 1 cell - A leader register is not a control: it renders props, ships no script and holds no input, so there is no control state for `disabled` to be the absence of. `LEADER / DISABLED`

**100.** 1 cell - The leader's rhythm IS the leader: the dots run from the name to its figure and they are the row's rule. A tight step would close them. `LEADER / DENSE`

**101.** 1 cell - A leader is a register on the paper: inside a card its dots would be the card's rule, and the card is a record's surface. `LEADER / IN A CARD`

#### What the exploration changed

1. **DOCCONTENTS** - from `NINETY / DENSE`

    **Found.** A document with ninety sections spent the rail's whole head on its contents. `Doc/_Layout.scss` caps that head at 50% of the rail, so the register was a scroll box the reader had to scroll to find the section they were already in - and the tree, which is the rail's other half, was left a slit. The block could be dense or not; it could not be folded, and a page could not choose either.

    **Built.** `DocContents.collapsible` prints the rail register as a `&lt;details open&gt;` - one row carrying the label, the count and the way back in - and `DocLayout.contentsFold: "auto"` folds it above 24 rows, so the ninety-section document folds itself and the twelve-section one does not. Open by default: the fold exists so a reader can give the rail's scroll to the tree, not so a page can withhold its own contents. `dense` is the second half of the same answer - the same rows in less air.

2. **DOCCONTENTS** - from `NINETY / the marking itself`

    **Found.** The register marked the section the reader was in and the mark could be forty rows below the register's edge: present in the DOM, invisible on the screen. A marking that is not on screen is the one failure a marking can have, and it was the failure the ninety-section case produced.

    **Built.** `Doc/Contents.ts` gains `Reveal` - when the marked row is outside the scroll register it sits in, the register is scrolled to it, once, instantly. The register is found by walking up to the first ancestor that actually scrolls, so the rail's head and the clause rail are served by the same code and neither names the other's class. Instant, not smooth: the mark is a position, and the reader caused the change.

3. **FOLIO** - from `LONG`

    **Found.** The source already broke at its `/`s, with `&lt;wbr&gt;` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` behind them - and the PART did not: it was `white-space: nowrap`. A folio on a deep page prints `/DOC/DEEP-DIVE-FILESYSTEM-FOOTPRINT`, which at 13px tracked is wider than the card it closes, and a folio that runs past the band's right edge is the one thing a folio may never do: it is the mark that says the band has ended.

    **Built.** `Folio` splits the part at its own `/` separators and puts a `&lt;wbr&gt;` after each - the same break points the source carries, for the same reason - and `Detail/_Folio.scss` sets the part to `white-space: normal` with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` as the backstop for one segment longer than the band. A short part takes no break; the ordinal and the part still never part company, because the place group stays `nowrap` between them.

4. **DOCCARD** - from `NO SUMMARY / PARTIAL`

    **Found.** A page with no `description` printed a card with a title and nothing under it, in a grid where every other card had two lines. The card did not say the description was missing; it closed up, and a card two lines shorter than its neighbours reads as a card that failed to load - the exact adverse state the brief says must be designed rather than left to chance.

    **Built.** `DocCard.absent` prints `◎ DESCRIPTION: UNAVAILABLE` in the note's own slot, at the note's own size, in the meta voice - so the grid's rows keep their height and the missing fact is stated in the vocabulary's word rather than as a blank. `DocIndex` passes the same sentence into the card body's `RecordEntry`, so the index grid and the feature cards answer the same way.

5. **DOCCONTENTS** - from `REST / the grammar`

    **Found.** The register named itself and not its extent: `ON THIS PAGE` over twelve rows, `ON THIS PAGE` over ninety, with no figure anywhere - while every other counted line on the site prints `# LABEL / NN`. The one register a reader consults for orientation was the one register with no count.

    **Built.** `DocContents` derives the count from `Items.length` (never from a prop, so it cannot outlive the rows) and prints it one U+2001 after the label in both registers - the rail's head and the disclosure's summary. The separator is drawn by the stylesheet and belongs to the figure, so a wrapped label never opens a line with an em quad.

6. **DOCLAYER** - from `ONE SECTION / ONE`

    **Found.** A layer with one page printed nothing at all - `entries.length &gt; 1` was the only arm - so the one fact this block exists to give, how big the thing the reader just finished is, was the one fact a one-page layer could not give. The reader finished a section and was told nothing about it.

    **Built.** `DocLayer` renders at `entries.length &gt;= 1`: above one it is the disclosure it always was, at exactly one it is the same row with the same label, value and count and no glyph - because there is nothing to open. `unitOne` lets the count read `01 PAGE` without the block pluralising a word it was handed.

7. **RUSTVIEWER** - from `EMPTY / WITH ACTION`

    **Found.** With no crates the viewer printed an empty tab bar and an `&lt;iframe&gt;` with no `src`: a frame around nothing, which is the composition a reader reads as broken rather than as absent. And the bar was a `role="tablist"` whose only keyboard path was Tab - the ARIA pattern it claimed was not implemented, so the arrows did nothing and a keyboard reader could not walk the crates.

    **Built.** `RustViewer.empty` prints the absence inside the frame's own box - `◎`, the sentence and the line that says why - and the frame is not rendered at all. The tab bar gains the pattern it promised: roving `tabindex`, ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down, Home and End, focus following the selection. `STATUS: LOADING` prints above the frame until it loads and the script removes it.

8. **DOCARTICLE** - from `EMPTY / LOADING / ERROR`

    **Found.** An article whose prose did not render printed its breadcrumb, its kicker, its `h1`, its strip and then a white card with nothing in it. Every other block in the family had its two adverse arms; the shell that holds all of them had none, so the one page that is nothing but paper was the one page that could be blank paper.

    **Built.** `DocArticle.state` (`rest` | `empty` | `loading`) with `empty` and `keys`: `empty` prints `◎`, the page's sentence and `STATUS: UNAVAILABLE` inside the paper; `loading` prints the keys with their values barred. `ReadingDocument` gains the same two arms, so the legal set cannot print a blank clause card either.

9. **DOCAPPENDIX** - from `EMPTY / PARTIAL / LOADING`

    **Found.** The three closing artifacts printed their `h2`, their lede and then whatever the build had: an appendix whose rows were not read was a heading and a sentence over a hole, and the architecture panel with no `Index` printed an empty `&lt;ul&gt;` under a lede about the fifteen elements.

    **Built.** `DocAppendix.state` with `empty`/`loading` arms under the same heading and lede, and a partial arm for the strip: an architecture panel with no `Index` prints `◎ STATUS: UNAVAILABLE` rather than an empty badge run. The panel's sentence is never dropped, because the subject is still stated when its destinations are not.

10. **DOCLAYOUT** - from `EMPTY`

**Found.** A rail with no sections printed its title and then nothing - a label over a hole, in both the rail and the narrow-viewport panel. The one navigation a documentation page has said `Documentation` and stopped.

**Built.** `DocLayout` prints `◎` and `sidebar.empty`'s sentence where the tree would be, in the rail and in the panel, at the panel's own inset. The head, the tree's slot and the foot keep their places, so the rail still reads as a rail.

11. **SEE** - from `LOADING / NO X-REF`

**Found.** The block refused the empty frame - correctly - and therefore had no way to say the other thing: that the references were asked for and not read. A foot in that state printed its folio alone, and a reader could not tell a band with no cross-references from a build that never read them.

**Built.** `See.state="loading"` prints the register and its keys with the values barred; `BandFoot.seeState` forwards it, so the foot keeps its two ends and its rule. The resting arm is unchanged: no references still renders nothing at all.

#### What its matrix does not ask

5 conditions, 70 cells unanswered - `MISSING`, `DENIED`, `IN A BAND`, `NO ACTION`, `REDUCED`. The family's matrix has no column for these, and `/Specimen/States` §THE UNASKED prints the sentence that says why.

#### Its live rows

- **/THE DOCUMENTS** - The shell that holds a reading column, in the four shapes the brief named: a resting article, an article with no summary, a title wider than the rail, and the same shell with no rail at all - plus the rail with one section, with ninety, and with no tree.
- **/THE CONTENTS** - The page's own contents in every register it has: the pinned rail, the fold, the dense step, one section, a heading wider than the rail, the disclosure, and the rows on their own at ninety.
- **/THE INDEX** - The manual's filing: a chapter and its count, a chapter holding a page with no description, a chapter of sixteen, the card alone in its three arms, the three appendices and the crate viewer - including the one the brief asked for by name, an index card with a missing description.
- **/THE DETAIL** - The apparatus that closes a band: the foot at rest, with no cross-references, with its references unread, inside a card and at 640px; the folio under a long source and a long part; the see-also in its three arms; and the leader at one entry, at thirty-eight and in a narrow column.
- **/THE READING** - The surface the legal set wears: read with its clause rail, read straight through with no rail, and read with no standfirst, where the facts become the opening.
- **/THE ADVERSE** - The seven compositions a reader meets when the world is unkind: an empty paper and a loading one, an empty document and a loading one, an empty register and a loading one, and the leader at 640px where the dots are the only rule it has.

---

### `# 08` /THE COMPOSITION

**For.** The marketing layer is a LAYER, not a block: thirty-five `Dynamic/*` parts were built to be the schema between content and surface, and a part with no importer is a decision the owner has not made yet.

**Read for.** The hero, the bands, the cards, the manifest, the marks, the verdict on every `Dynamic/*` part, and sixty-six live compositions - a hero with no evidence image, a proof band of three, nine tiles in a narrow card, a seal at 16px and at 240px.

**Its boundary.** The composition family asks the marketing layer's own shapes - no plate, three, nine, at 16, at 240, lone, no action - and asks `NO ACTION` where the other families ask `WITH ACTION`. It leaves the motion arm and the positive action to the blocks it composes: a hero is a page's first sentence, and a first sentence does not animate.

#### What it may never be

The strongest 4 of the 487 sentences this
family's matrix uses to mark a combination impossible. The numbering is the
family's, and the matrix below references it cell by cell.

1. **39 cells.** Nine tiles is the stack's composition.

    `ROADMAPBAND / NINE / RELEASECARD / NINE / PLATFORMCARD / NINE / WORKINGBAND / NINE / FIELDRECORDDATACARD / NINE / FIELDRECORDMETADATA / NINE / FIELDRECORDACTION / NINE / FIELDRECORDSTATUS / NINE / FIELDRECORDEVIDENCE / NINE / SEMANTICLEDGER / NINE / DYNAMICHEADER / NINE / DYNAMICFOOTER / NINE / DYNAMICPORTAL / NINE / DYNAMICTRANSPARENCY / NINE / DYNAMICVERIFICATIONINFO / NINE / ACCOUNTPAGE / NINE / AUTH0ACCOUNT / NINE / AUTH0ACCOUNTGATE / NINE / AUTH0CALLBACKHANDLER / NINE / VERIFYPAGE / NINE / DYNAMICACCOUNTPROFILE / NINE / DYNAMICDASHBOARDUSER / NINE / DYNAMICLOCALFIRSTSCAN / NINE / DYNAMICAUTHHEADER / NINE / DYNAMICAUTHSTATUS / NINE / DYNAMICSTATEPORT / NINE / DYNAMICSIGNIN / NINE / DYNAMICSIGNUP / NINE / DYNAMICFORGOTPASSWORD / NINE / DYNAMICRESETPASSWORD / NINE / DYNAMICEMAILVERIFICATION / NINE / DYNAMICCONTACTFORM / NINE / DYNAMICINPUT / NINE / DYNAMICCHECKBOX / NINE / DYNAMICBUTTON / NINE / DYNAMICCARD / NINE / DYNAMICTABLE / NINE / DYNAMICRICHTEXT / NINE / MERMAIDFALLBACK / NINE`

#### The row that proves it

| MARK     | STATE       | PART         |
| -------- | ----------- | ------------ |
| `CMP_22` | NO ARTEFACT | PLATFORMBAND |

**When it is right.** The day nothing is downloadable: the plate keeps its surface and states `ARTIFACTS: UNAVAILABLE`, why, and `CHANNEL: SOURCE`.

**Why this row.** The marketing layer's honest worst case is a product with nothing to download: the plate keeps its surface and states `ARTIFACTS: UNAVAILABLE`, why, and `CHANNEL: SOURCE`, instead of an empty frame.

**See it.** `/Specimen/States` - the family's row on the states gallery; `/Specimen#composition` - the family's own matrix.
